Answer ends at the first full stop ('sufficit.'); what follows ('Avarus ex eo dictus, quod sit avidus auri...') turns to a new lemma and no longer answers the question.

question: Rusticus es?
answer: nescis quid Graeco nomine dicar: spuma vocor nitri.
derivation: Quoted Martial couplet on aphronitrum, introduced by Isidore's framing 'De quo quidam ait', which is dropped as a speech tag. The speaker poses the question 'Rusticus es?' and answers it himself: if you are a rustic, you do not know the Greek name, so I am called (Latin) 'spuma nitri'. Window ends at the full stop after 'spuma vocor nitri'; what follows ('Graecus es? aphronitrum.') is the parallel second question/answer, taken as a separate pair.

question: Graecus es?
answer: aphronitrum.
derivation: Second clause of the same Martial couplet: the speaker asks 'Graecus es?' and answers with the Greek name 'aphronitrum'. Starts after the full stop following 'spuma vocor nitri'; nothing follows in the couplet (the verse-line / footer scaffolding is excluded).

question: Quare inter ceteras liberales disciplinas Medicinae ars non contineatur?
answer: Propterea, quia illae singulares continent causas, ista vero omnium.
derivation: Authorial self-posed question. Dropped the framing narration 'Quaeritur a quibusdam' (narrates the asking), keeping the indirect-question clause 'quare inter ceteras liberales disciplinas Medicinae ars non contineatur' as the interrogative; normalized capitalization of the first word and added a terminal '?'. Answer ends at the first full stop: 'Propterea, quia illae singulares continent causas, ista vero omnium.' What follows ('Nam et Grammaticam medicus scire debet...') begins elaboration of why medicine touches all disciplines, so it is excluded. Stripped the section marker '[1]' scaffolding.

question: Quid sit ius naturale?
answer: Ius naturale est, aut civile, aut gentium.
derivation: Chapter heading 'QVID SIT IVS NATVRALE' is a genuine interrogative posed and answered by Isidore. First-word capitalization kept; terminal '?' supplied. Answer is the opening sentence of the body; the bracketed editorial supplement '[est]' is stripped keeping the word 'est'. Window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Ius naturale est commune omnium nationum...') elaborates with examples rather than giving the direct division.

question: Quid sit ius civile?
answer: Ius civile est quod quisque populus vel civitas sibi proprium humana divinaque causa constituit.
derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS CIVILE' is an interrogative; the single-sentence body answers it. The chapter contains only this one sentence, so the whole body is the answer. Terminal '?' supplied on the question.

question: Quid sit ius gentium?
answer: Ius gentium est sedium occupatio, aedificatio, munitio, bella, captivitates, servitutes, postliminia, foedera pacis, indutiae, legatorum non violandorum religio, conubia inter alienigenas prohibita.
derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS GENTIVM' answered by the opening definitional sentence. Window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Et inde ius gentium, quia eo iure...') is an etymological aside, not the definition.

question: Quid sit ius militare?
answer: Ius militare est belli inferendi sollemnitas, foederis faciendi nexus, signo data egressio in hostem vel commissio.
derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS MILITARE' answered by the opening definitional clause. Window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Item signo dato receptio...') continues enumerating further items rather than giving the core definition.

question: Quid sit ius publicum?
answer: Ius publicum est in sacris et sacerdotibus, in magistratibus.
derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS PVBLICVM' answered by the chapter's single sentence (the whole body). Terminal '?' supplied on the question.

question: Quid sit ius Quiritum?
answer: Ius Quiritum est proprie Romanorum, quo nulli tenentur nisi Quirites, id est Romani, tamquam de legitimis hereditatibus, de cretionibus, de tutelis, de usucapionibus.
derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS QVIRITVM' answered by the opening definitional sentence. Window ends at the first full stop ('...de usucapionibus.'); what follows ('quae iura apud alium nullum populum reperiuntur...') is elaboration on the same.

question: Quid sit lex?
answer: Lex est constitutio populi, qua maiores natu simul cum plebibus aliquid sanxerunt.
derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT LEX' is an interrogative answered by the chapter's single defining sentence (the whole body). Terminal '?' supplied on the question.

question: Quis est iste rex gloriae?
answer: Dominus virtutum.
derivation: Verbatim Psalm 23,10 quoted by Isidore to gloss 'Sabaoth'. The quoted verse itself is a genuine interrogative ('Who is this king of glory?') immediately answered ('The Lord of hosts'). Stripped the section marker [7], the scriptural-citation framing 'de quo in Psalmo ab angelis dicitur (23,10):' and the enclosing quotation marks. Nothing omitted between question and answer; the answer is the entire reply.

question: Deus autem, qui non est factus, quomodo est perfectus?
answer: Sed hoc vocabulum de usu nostro sumpsit humana inopia, sicut et reliqua verba, quatenus id quod ineffabile est utcumque dici possit, quoniam de Deo nihil digne humanus sermo dicit, sicut sunt et alia.
derivation: Authorial rhetorical question: having noted 'perfectio' implies completion of something made, Isidore asks how God, who was not made, can be called perfect. Kept the preceding clause 'Deus autem, qui non est factus' so 'perfectus' has its subject. The answer is the operative reply opening section [32] ('but human poverty took this word from our usage...'); ran to its full stop. Stripped section markers [31] and [32].

question: Cur autem eum capite canino fingunt?
answer: Quod inter omnia animalia canis sagacissimum genus et perspicax habeatur.
derivation: Authorial rhetorical question and self-answer about Hermes Trismegistus, depicted with a dog's head. The interrogative 'Cur autem eum capite canino fingunt' is taken as the question; 'eum' refers to Hermes from the preceding sentence ('Hermes autem Graece dicitur ... ter maximus nominatus est'), which is left out as setup because the etymological/euhemeristic context makes the depicted figure clear. The framing 'haec ratio dicitur' ('this is said to be the reason'), which narrates that the answer follows, is dropped; the operative answering clause 'quod inter omnia animalia canis sagacissimum genus et perspicax habeatur' genuinely answers 'cur'. Capitalization of 'Quod' normalized; terminal comma replaced by period.

question: Qua lingua angeli loquantur?
answer: Non quod angelorum aliquae linguae sint, sed hoc per exaggerationem dicitur.
derivation: Authorial question posed via the framing 'Vbi quaeritur' (dropped as narration of the asking) following the Pauline quotation 'Si linguis hominum loquar et angelorum.' The interrogative clause 'qua lingua angeli loquantur' is normalized to a direct question with capital Q and '?'. The answer is the author's own resolution that immediately follows the semicolon ('non quod angelorum aliquae linguae sint, sed hoc per exaggerationem dicitur'); section continues into [13] with a separate new question.

question: Qua lingua in futurum homines loquantur?
answer: Nusquam reperitur.
derivation: Authorial question posed via the framing 'Item quaeritur' (dropped as narration of the asking); the indirect-question clause 'qua lingua in futurum homines loquantur' is normalized to a direct question. The answer is the author's own 'nusquam reperitur' (it is found nowhere) immediately after the colon; cut before the following supporting citation 'Nam dicit Apostolus (1 Cor. 13,8): Sive linguae, cessabunt,' which is justification, not the answer.

question: De consummatione alicuius facti dicitur perfectio. Deus autem qui non est factus quomodo est perfectus?
answer: Sed hunc sermonem de usu nostro sumit humana inopia, sicut et reliqua uerba, quatenus id quod ineffabile est utcumque dici possit, quoniam de Deo nihil digne humanus sermo dicit.
derivation: Author poses and answers his own puzzle. Kept the preceding sentence (De consummatione... perfectio) as verbatim setup so the question's term perfectus has a referent. Answer is the full reply sentence (to its first and only full stop); nothing trimmed.

question: Quid faciebat Deus antequam caelum faceret? Cur noua uoluntas in Deo ut mundum conderet orta est?
answer: Sed noua in Deo uoluntas exorta non est, quia etsi in re mundus non erat, in aeterna tamen ratione et consilio semper erat.
derivation: Dropped the framing tag Quidam aiunt: (meta-narration of the asking). The two interrogatives are quoted objections that the author answers in his own voice. Answer is the single reply sentence to its full stop; it directly rebuts the second question and resolves both.

question: Si Deum angeli contuentur et uident, cur Petrus apostolus dicit: In quem desiderant angeli Dei conspicere? Item, si eum non contuentur, nec uident, quomodo, iuxta sententiam Domini, angeli eorum semper uident faciem Patris qui est in caelis?
answer: Sed bene utrumque est: nam ueraciter credimus quod Deum angeli et uident, et uidere desiderant; et habent, et habere festinant; et amant et amare nituntur.
derivation: Two genuine interrogatives (cur... / quomodo...) the author raises and resolves. Answer ends at the first full stop (Sed bene utrumque est... amare nituntur); the following elaboration (Si enim sic uidere desiderant...) digresses and is cut. Internal semicolons retained per the to-the-first-full-stop rule.

question: Quare non possunt animalia bruta interrogare?
answer: Quia nesciunt ratiocinare.
derivation: Direct Quare question answered immediately by quia nesciunt ratiocinare. question: Sed cur futura quasi praeterita scribuntur?
answer: Nisi quia ea quae adhuc facienda sunt in opere, iam facta sunt in diuina praedestinatione.

Normalized the run-on into question + answer at the natural break; capitalized Nisi and set terminal punctuation. No words added or reordered.

question: Sed cur quae adhuc facienda erant iam facta narrantur?
answer: Quia quae nobis adhuc futura sunt, apud Dei aeternitatem iam facta sunt.

question: Quid enim ex se ille latro meruit, qui de faucibus crucem ascendit, de cruce paradisum adiit?

question: Dum apostolus dicat: Non est potestas nisi a Deo, quomodo Dominus per prophetam de quibusdam potestatibus dicit: Ipsi regnauerunt, sed non ex me, quasi diceret non me propitio, etiamsi me irato?

question: Quid metuis turbae decreta severae?
answer: Causa meo tantum competit ista foro.

question: Animae, an carnis resurrectionem dicis?
answer: Non solius animae, sed carnis, quae cum anima renascitur in lavacro.

question: Quid igitur faciam?
answer: Quod inplere non possum, negare non audeo.

answer: Sine culpa veniam postulabo rectius arbitrans pacem loco motus petere, quam aequo gradu certamina concitare.

question: Quorsum ista tam alto repetita principio et ita procul coepta, ut merito quivis Horatiano de nobis possit sale ludere: et "gemino bellum Troianum orditur ab ovo"?

AP 147] following the embedded quote is stripped. Answer is the operative reply; window ends at the full stop before 'ecce iam centenarius...', where he turns to praising Paulus's vigor. question: Vbi tamdiu moratus es, pater?
answer: Vae mihi peccatori, qui falsum monachi nomen fero. Vidi Eliam, uidi Ioannem in deserto, et uere in paradiso Paulum uidi.

The whole reply is two sentences forming one continuous answer to where he had been; it is kept entire. What follows ('Ac sic ore compresso...') is narration and is cut.

question: In quot primas partes legis diuinae scientia diuiditur?
answer: In duas, quarum una ad ipsam superficiem dictionis proprie pertinet, alia in rebus est quas ipsa scriptura nos edocet.

question: Species dictionis quot sunt?
answer: Quattuor: nam aut historica est aut prophetica aut prouerbialis aut simpliciter docens.

question: Historia quid est?
answer: Praeteritarum rerum praesentiumue narratio.

question: Quid est prophetia?
answer: Rerum latentium praeteritarum aut praesentium aut futurarum ex diuina inspiratione manifestatio.
derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative definition-question answered by the disciple's complete defining sentence.

question: Quae est prouerbialis species?
answer: Quaedam figurata locutio, aliud sonans, aliud sentiens, et in praesenti commonens tempore.
derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative question, complete self-contained answer to the full stop.

question: Quae est simplex doctrina?

derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative definition-question; the disciple's full reply answers it directly.

answer: Vis animi inuiolata siue spontanea, secundum quam diuersae atque contrariae cogitationes efficiuntur et opera.

question: Quam uocamus acceptionem, siue uocationem?
answer: Eam scilicet qua Deus quosdam homines uel populos specialis gratiae beneficio sibi conciliare dignatur, plusque circa eos quam circa ceteros homines diuinae indulgentiae et quasi familiares fauores ostendit.
derivation: Stripped the [Delta]/[Mu] speaker labels. Interrogative definition-question; the disciple's whole self-contained reply answers it, to the full stop.

question: Quid est ergo typus, siue figura?
answer: Praesentium aut praeteritarum aut futurarum rerum ignotarum per opera, secundum id quod opera sunt, manifestatio.

answer: Futurarum incertarum rerum uerbis, in quantum uerba sunt, manifestatio.

question: Si condicio ponatur, utrius vitae sortem legant, hesterni laboris an praesentium epularum?

question: Quem imperii faciat heredem?
answer: Dignissimum.

The embedded indirect question 'quem imperii faciat heredem' is the author's verbatim words, normalized to capital Q and terminal '?'. The answer 'dignissimum' is verbatim; the stray '?' before it is a conversion artifact (stripped), and capitalization/terminal stop normalized. This is a genuine interrogative genuinely answered.

question: Quos autem homines Romanos esse?
answer: Nempe pastores, qui latrocinio iustis dominis ademptum solum teneant, qui uxores cum propter originis dehonestamenta non invenirent, vi publica rapuerint, qui denique urbem ipsam parricidio condiderint murorumque fundamenta fraterno sanguine adsperserint.

What follows the cut is section 11, 'Aetolos autem principes Graeciae semper fuisse...', which turns from describing the Romans to praising the Aetolians and so is not part of the answer.

question: Sed adversus Hannibalem ducem quis melius quam Africani frater crearetur, cum vincere Poenos opus Scipionum esset?
answer: Creatur igitur consul Lucius Scipio, eique datur legatus frater Africanus.

Answer taken to its first full stop: 'Creatur igitur consul Lucius Scipio, eique datur legatus frater Africanus' — the operative answer (Lucius Scipio elected, with Africanus as legate). Cut before 'ut intellegeret Antiochus...', which elaborates the purpose rather than answering.

question: Quare enim iste usus fructus sibi tale vindicat privilegium, ut generali interemptione usus fructus ipse solus excipiatur?

question: Quare enim, si filius familias fuerit is qui usum fructum habet, forte ex castrensi peculio, ubi nec usus fructus adquiritur ei, possessum, per emancipationem eum amittat?
answer: Sed secundum quod definitum est tunc eum tantummodo desinere, cum usufructuarius vel res pereat, et tantummodo eum cum anima vel rei substantia expirare, nisi praedictae exceptionis vigor reclamaverit.
derivation: Prose legal text; authorial rhetorical question with its own answer. Stripped the section marker (CJ.3.33.16.2: Imperator Justinianus) and the trailing subscript apparatus (<a 530 d. k. oct. ... conss.>). The preceding sentence 'Sed nec per omnem capitis deminutionem ... subiectis.' is general framing not needed for the question, so it was not included. The answer is the reply's independent sentence (beginning 'Sed secundum quod definitum est'), taken to the first full stop, which genuinely answers the 'why should he lose it' (he loses it only on death/destruction, not by emancipation). question: Si quis servum certi nominis aut quandam solidorum quantitatem vel aliam rem promiserit et, cum licentia ei fuerat unum ex his solvendo liberari, utrumque per ignorantiam dependerit, dubitabatur, cuius rei datur a legibus ei repetitio, utrumne servi an pecuniae, et utrum stipulator an promissor habeat huius rei facultatem?
answer: Nobis haec decidentibus iuliani et papiniani placet sententia, ut ipse habeat electionem recipiendi, qui et dandi habuit.

question: Pro dubietate eorum, qui mente titubante indebitam solverunt pecuniam, certamen legislatoribus incidit, utrumne id, quod ancipiti animo persolverunt, possint repetere an non?
answer: Quod nos decidentes sancimus omnibus, qui incerto animo indebitam dederunt pecuniam vel aliam quandam speciem persolverunt, repetitionem non denegari et praesumptionem transactionis non contra eos induci, nisi hoc specialiter ab altera parte approbetur.

Actor-line and date footer dropped as scaffolding. The answer is the whole single-sentence resolution in CJ.4.5.11.1, which directly settles the question (recovery is not denied).

question: Si duo vel plures communem servum habeant et unus ex his iussit, ut nomine suo servus ab aliquo stipuletur decem puta aureos vel aliam rem, ipse autem servus non eius nomine qui iussit, sed alicuius ex dominis suis mentionem fecit et nomine illius stipulatus est, inter antiquam sapientiam quaerebatur, cui adquiritur actio et lucrum, quod ex hac accidit causa, utrumne ei qui iussit an ei cuius servus mentionem fecit an ambobus?
answer: Nobis verior eorum sententia videtur, qui domino qui iussit adferunt stipulationem et ei tantummodo adquiri dixerunt, quam aliorum, qui in alias opiniones deferuntur.

Actor-line and date footer excluded as scaffolding. question: Hermaphroditum cui comparamus?
answer: Et magis puto eius sexus aestimandum, qui in eo praevalet.

Dropped the framing 'Quaeritur:' ('it is asked') which narrates the asking, capitalized the first word of the now-leading interrogative. Answer is the jurist's direct reply, a single sentence ending at the full stop.

question: Si adrogator decesserit impubere relicto filio adoptivo et mox impubes decedat, an heredes adrogatoris teneantur?
answer: Et dicendum est heredes quoque restituturus et bona adrogati et praeterea quartam partem.

question: Si servus quamdiu latuit, dignitate praetoria functus sit, quid dicemus? quae edixit, quae decrevit, nullius fore momenti? an fore propter utilitatem eorum, qui apud eum egerunt vel lege vel quo alio iure?

question: Si communem fundum ego et tu habemus et vicinum fundum ego solus, an finium regundorum iudicium accipere possumus?
answer: Non posse nos accipere, quia ego et socius meus in hac actione adversarii esse non possumus, sed unius loco habemur.

question: Si heres unus, cum sub condicione adiectum coheredem aut apud hostes haberet, dixerit se heredem esse et actione expertus vicerit, deinde condicio heredis exstiterit vel postliminio redierit, an victoriae commodum debeat cum eo communicare?
answer: Et electionem coheredi dandam, id est aut communicandam eam aut experiundi faciendam potestatem huic, qui post victoriam coheredis effectus sit heres aut reversus sit in civitatem.

question: Fundus mihi communis est pupillae coheredi: in eo fundo reliquiae sunt conditae, quibus religio ab utriusque patribus debebatur, nam parentes quoque eiusdem pupillae ibi sepulti sunt: sed tutores distrahere fundum volunt: ego non consentio, sed portionem meam possidere malo, cum universitatem emere non possim et velim pro meo arbitrio exsequi ius religionis. An recte arbitrum communi dividundo ad hunc fundum partiendum petam an etiam is arbiter, qui familiae erciscundae datur, isdem partibus fungi possit, ut hanc possessionem exemptis ceteris corporibus hereditariis pro iure cuique nobis partiatur?
answer: Nihil proponi, cur familiae erciscundae iudicio addictus arbiter officium suum etiam in eius fundi de quo agitur divisionem interponere non possit: sed religiosa loca in iudicium non deduci eorumque ius singulis heredibus in solidum competere.

question: Pomponius philadelphus dotis causa praedia filiae quam habebat in potestate tradidit et reditus eorum genero solvi mandavit: an ea praecipua filia retinere possit, cum omnes filios heredes instituisset?

answer: Ex quo perdiderit fructuarius usum fructum, aestimabuntur in petitione fructus.

question: In alieno fundo, quem titius bona fide mercatus fuerat, frumentum sevi: an titius bonae fidei emptor perceptos fructus suos faciat?
answer: Fructus qui ex fundo percipiuntur intellegi debet propius ea accedere, quae servi operis suis adquirunt, quoniam in percipiendis fructibus magis corporis ius ex quo percipiuntur quam seminis, ex quo oriuntur aspicitur: et ideo nemo umquam dubitavit, quin, si in meo fundo frumentum tuum severim, segetes et quod ex messibus collectum fuerit meum fieret.

The framing tag 'respondi, quod' is dropped as narration of the reply; the answer begins at the operative 'Fructus qui...' (capitalized) and runs to the first full stop at 'meum fieret'. question: Quid ergo: si et filius familias et pater ex persona eius teneatur ( sive iussu eius contractum est sive in rem versum est patris vel in peculium), cuius persona circa moram spectabitur?
answer: Et si quidem pater dumtaxat convenietur, ex mora sua non tenetur: in filium tamen dabitur actio in hoc, ut quod minus a patre actor consecutus est, filius praestet: quod si filius moram fecerit, tunc actor vel cum ipso in solidum vel cum patre dumtaxat de peculio habebit.

question: Item si dividere fundum tecum velim, tu nolis et colam, an fructus dividi debeant post deductionem impensarum?
answer: Et puto dividendos.

question: Traiecticia ea pecunia est quae trans mare vehitur: ceterum si eodem loci consumatur, non erit traiecticia. An merces ex ea pecunia comparatae in ea causa habentur?
answer: Et interest, utrum etiam ipsae periculo creditoris navigent: tunc enim traiecticia pecunia fit.

question: Quingenta testamento tibi legata sunt: idem scriptum est in codicillis postea scriptis: refert, duplicare legatum voluerit an repetere et oblitus se in testamento legasse id fecerit: ab utro ergo probatio eius rei exigenda est?

question: Cum de indebito quaeritur, quis probare debet non fuisse debitum?
answer: Res ita temperanda est, ut, si quidem is, qui accepisse dicitur rem vel pecuniam indebitam, hoc negaverit et ipse qui dedit legitimis probationibus solutionem adprobaverit, sine ulla distinctione ipsum, qui negavit sese pecuniam accepisse, si vult audiri, compellendum esse ad probationes praestandas, quod pecuniam debitam accepit: per etenim absurdum est eum, qui ab initio negavit pecuniam suscepisse, postquam fuerit convictus eam accepisse, probationem non debiti ab adversario exigere.

question: Quod si non sit deprehensa, damnata autem, idcirco notetur, quia publico iudicio damnata est, at si deprehensa quidem sit, damnata autem non sit, notata erit?
answer: Ego puto, etsi absoluta sit post deprehensionem, adhuc tamen notam illi obesse debere, quia verum est eam in adulterio deprehensam, quia factum lex, non sententiam notaverit.

question: Fiunt autem res mariti, si constante matrimonio in dotem dentur. Quid ergo, si ante matrimonium?

question: Vir ab eo, qui uxori eius dotem facere volebat, certam pecuniam eo nomine stipulatus est, deinde acceptam eam fecit: essetne ea pecunia in dotem?
answer: Cum vero acceptam fecit, omnimodo periculum ad eum pertinebit: perinde enim est, ac si acceperit pecuniam et eandem promissori donaverit.

question: Quantae pecuniae dotem promittenti adultae mulieri curator consensum accommodare debeat?
answer: Modus ex facultatibus et dignitate mulieris maritique statuendus est, quousque ratio patitur.

question: Uxor viro usum fructum dotis nomine dedit, manente matrimonio eidem fundum vendidit: divortio facto quid dotis iudicio reciperare debeat?
answer: Dixi referre, quanti fundus venisset: nam si nudae proprietatis aestimatio facta fuisset, mulier dotis iudicio pretium usus fructus reciperare debet.

question: Si pacta sit mulier vel ante nuptias vel post nuptias, ut ex fundi fructibus quem dedit in dotem creditor mulieris dimittatur, an valeat pactum?
answer: Dico, si ante nuptias id convenerit, valere pactum eoque modo minorem dotem constitutam: post nuptias vero cum onera matrimonii fructus relevaturi sunt, iam de suo maritus paciscitur ut dimittat creditorem, et erit mera donatio.

question: Cum maritus, qui aestimata praedia in dotem acceperat, manente matrimonio pactus est circumscribendae mulieris gratia, ut praedia inaestimata essent, ut sine periculo suo ea deteriora faceret: an secundum priores dotales tabulas praedia aestimata remanerent et periculum eorum ad maritum pertineret?
answer: Respondi non idcirco pactum de quo quaereretur impediri, quod in matrimonio factum esset, si deteriore loco dos non esset: nihilo minus eo pacto admisso, si deteriora praedia faceret, eo etiam nomine dotis eum actione teneri.

question: Titius mulieris nomine dotem dedit et stipulatus est in casum mortis et divortii: divortio secuto non repetita dote titius decessit: mulier ex voluntate heredis eius redintegravit matrimonium: an ex stipulatu dotem petere possit?
answer: Respondi heredem titii, si consensisset, ut ea quantitas, quam ex stipulatu consequi potuerat, dotis reconciliato matrimonio fieret, posse pacti exceptione summoveri.

question: Mulier de dote quam dedit pacta est, ut, si in matrimonio decessisset, fratri eius redderetur isque in eum casum stipulatus est: mulier decedens quasdam res dotales marito legavit et aliis, quosdam ex servis dotalibus manumisit: an maritus earum nomine, quas legavit mulier, et servorum, quos manumisit, fratri tenetur?
answer: Respondi nihil proponi, cur non teneretur, cum et iam heredes defunctae tam legatariis quam libertatibus obnoxii sint.

question: Si mulier acceptam a marito pecuniam in sportulas pro cognato suo ordini erogaverit, an donatio valeat?
answer: Valere nec videri locupletiorem mulierem factam.

question: Vir uxori pecuniam cum donare vellet, permisit ei, ut a debitore suo stipuletur: illa cum id fecisset, priusquam pecuniam auferret, divortium fecit: utrum vir eam summam petere debeat an ea promissione propter donationis causam actio nulla esset?
answer: Inanem fuisse eam stipulationem.

question: Mulier, quae ad communem filium volebat, qui in potestate patris erat, post mortem patris fundum pervenire, eum patri tradidit, uti post mortem restituatur filio. An donatio tibi videatur, ut nihil agatur, an valeat quidem, sed mulieri potestas datur, si noluerit, eum repetere?
answer: Si color vel titulus, ut sic dixerim, donationi quaesitus est, nihil valebit traditio.

question: Ea, quae a marito suo pecuniam ex causa donationis acceperat, litteras ad eum misit huiusmodi: cum petenti mihi a te, domine carissime, adnuerit indulgentia tua viginti ad expediendas quasdam res meas, quae summa mihi numerata est sub ea condicione, ut, si per me meosque mores quid steterit, quo minus in diem vitae nostrae matrimonium permaneat, sive invito te discessero de domo tua vel repudium tibi sine ulla querella misero divortiumque factum per me probabitur, tunc viginti, quae mihi hac die donationis causa dare voluisti, daturam restituturam me sine ulla dilatione: spondeo. An, si eadem titio marito suo repudium miserit, pecuniam restituere debeat?
answer: Pecuniam, quam vir uxori donavit, ex stipulatione proposita, si condicio eius exstitit, peti posse, quoniam ex donatione in pecuniam creditam conversa est.

question: Si praedia et mancipia seiae data effecta sint eius tempore concubinatus ac postea tempore matrimonii aliis acceptis reddita sunt, quid iuris est?

question: Filius rebus matris intervenire solitus pecunia matris consentiente ipsa mancipia et res mercatus emptionum instrumenta suo nomine confecit: decessit in patris potestate. An mater cum marito suo experiri et qua actione uti possit?
answer: Si mater obligatum filium in ea pecunia voluit esse, intra annum, quam filius decessit, de peculio cum patre, in cuius potestate fuisse proponatur, actionem habere.

question: Seia sempronio cum certa die nuptura esset, antequam domum deduceretur tabulaeque dotis signarentur, donavit tot aureos: an ea donatio rata sit?
answer: Itaque nisi ante matrimonium contractum, quod consensu intellegitur, donatio facta esset, non valere.

question: Virgini in hortos deductae ante diem tertium quam ibi nuptiae fierent, cum in separata diaeta ab eo esset, die nuptiarum, priusquam ad eum transiret et priusquam aqua et igni acciperetur, id est nuptiae celebrentur, optulit decem aureos dono: post nuptias contractas divortio facto an summa donata repeti possit?
answer: Id, quod ante nuptias donatum proponeretur, non posse de dote deduci.

question: Titia divortium a seio fecit: hanc titius in sua potestate esse dicit et dotem sibi reddi postulat: ipsa se matrem familias dicit et de dote agere vult: quae partes iudicis sint?
answer: Patri, nisi probet filiam non solum in sua potestate esse, sed etiam consentire sibi, denegandam actionem.

question: Lucius titius filiae suae nomine centum doti promisit gaio seio: inter gaium seium et lucium titium patrem mulieris convenit, ne dos a viro vivo lucio titio id est patre mulieris, peteretur: postea culpa mariti divortio facto solutum est matrimonium et pater mulieris decedens alios heredes instituit filia exheredata: an ab heredibus soceri maritus exigere dotem potest, cum eam mulieri redditurus est?
answer: Cum filia aliis a patre heredibus institutis actionem de dote sua reciperanda habere coeperit, necesse habebit maritus aut exactam dotem aut actiones ei praestare.

question: Gaius seius avus maternus seiae nepti, quae erat in patris potestate, certam pecuniae quantitatem dotis nomine lucio titio marito dedit et instrumento dotali huiusmodi pactum et stipulationem complexus est: si inter lucium titium maritum et seiam divortium sine culpa mulieris factum esset, dos omnis seiae uxori vel gaio seio avo materno redderetur restituereturque. Cum seius avus maternus statim vita defunctus sit et seia postea sine culpa sua divorterit vivo patre suo, in cuius potestate est, an et cui actio ex hoc pacto et stipulatione competat et utrum heredi avi materni ex stipulatu an nepti?
answer: In persona quidem neptis videri inutiliter stipulationem esse conceptam, quoniam avus maternus ei stipulatus proponitur.

question: Maevia marito suo inter alias res dotis etiam instrumentum solidorum decem tradidit, quo otacilius eidem maeviae caverat daturum se, cum nuptum ire coepisset, decem milia: ex eo instrumento maritus nihil exegit, quia nec potuit: si dos a marito petatur, an compellendus sit etiam illam summam, quae instrumento continetur, refundere?
answer: Potuisse quidem eum, cui actiones mandatae sunt, debitorem convenire: sed si sine dolo malo vel culpa exigere pecuniam non potuit, neque dotis nomine eum conveniri posse neque mandati iudicio.

question: Fundus aestimatus in dotem datus a creditore antecedente ex causa pignoris ablatus est: an mulier, si aestimationem dotis repetat, exceptione summovenda sit?

question: Aestimatis rebus in dotem datis pactum intercessit, ut, ex quacumque causa dos reddi deberet, ipsae res restituerentur habita ratione augmenti et deminutionis viri boni arbitratu, quae vero non exstarent, ab initio aestimatio earum: cum res quaedam quas maritus vendiderat exstarent, an secundum pactum et haec ad mulierem pertinerent?

question: Ubi ergo admittimus deminutionem dotis ipso iure fieri?

The question is the parenthetical interrogative 'quis enim magis alienam rem invito domino contrectat quam qui vi rapit?'; the preceding clause 'Qui res alienas rapit, tenetur quidem etiam furti' is kept verbatim as setup so 'eum' in the answer has a referent. The parentheses are presentational and dropped. The answer is the immediately following sentence 'ideoque recte dictum est, eum improbum furem esse', which resolves the rhetorical question (the violent robber is the worst sort of thief); it ends at the close of the parenthesis, before 'sed tamen propriam actionem eius delicti nomine praetor introduxit', which turns to a new point.

question: sed quo cecidit sub crimine? quisnam delator quibus indicibus, quo teste probauit?
answer: nil horum; uerbosa et grandis epistula uenit a Capreis.
derivation: A bystander in the crowd asks under what charge Sejanus fell and by what informer/evidence/witness; a second speaker answers 'none of these' and gives the real cause (a long letter from Capri). Question span starts at 'sed quo cecidit' (prior words 'numquam... amaui hunc hominem' are declarative aside, not part of the interrogative). Answer ends at 'a Capreis.'; what follows is the first speaker's rejoinder 'bene habet, nil plus interrogo' (a new statement, dropped).

question: exitus ergo quis est?
answer: uincitur idem nempe et in exilium praeceps fugit atque ibi magnus mirandusque cliens sedet ad praetoria regis, donec Bithyno libeat uigilare tyranno.
derivation: Author asks what then was Hannibal's end and answers it himself. The interjection 'o gloria!' immediately after the question is framing exclamation and is dropped. Answer begins at 'uincitur idem' and runs to the first full stop 'tyranno.'; the following 'finem animae...' sentence turns to a new elaboration about how he died, so it is cut.

question: longa dies igitur quid contulit?
answer: omnia uidit euersa et flammis Asiam ferroque cadentem.
derivation: Author asks what long life conferred on Priam and answers himself. Answer runs to the first full stop 'cadentem.'; the next sentence 'tunc miles tremulus...' continues the narrative of Priam's death and is cut as elaboration.

question: Nullane peiuri capitis fraudisque nefandae poena erit?
answer: Abreptum crede hunc grauiore catena protinus et nostro (quid plus uelit ira?) necari arbitrio.
derivation: An imagined interlocutor's quoted objection (a real interrogative, 'Will there be no punishment for the perjured and for foul fraud?') answered by the author. Stripped the dangling inline verse-number 175 that falls after 'catena'. The answer is the operative response granting maximal punishment; it ends at 'arbitrio' (source has a colon there). Cut what follows, 'manet illa tamen iactura nec umquam depositum tibi sospes erit...', which turns from answering to elaborating that the deposit is still lost. The interior '(quid plus uelit ira?)' is the author's own contiguous words and is kept. Normalized initial capital and terminal punctuation only.

question: Officium cras primo sole mihi peragendum in ualle Quirini. Quae causa officii?
answer: Nubit amicus nec multos adhibet.
derivation: Setup is the duty-claimant's speech 'officium cras primo sole mihi peragendum in ualle Quirini', giving 'officii' its referent; the author's interrogative 'quae causa officii?' is the real question. The reply opens 'quid quaeris?' (a non-answering deflection, 'why do you ask?'), which I cut at the start; the operative answer is 'nubit amicus nec multos adhibet'. Dropped the trailing 'liceat modo uiuere, fient...' which moves to authorial comment. Inline verse number 135 stripped.

question: Quid Romae faciam?
answer: Mentiri nescio.
derivation: Umbricius poses and answers his own question within his monologue. Question is the self-contained interrogative at line 41. The answer's operative response is 'mentiri nescio' (the first clause genuinely answering 'what would I do at Rome?'); it ends there where he turns from answering to elaborating with further examples ('librum, si malus est, nequeo laudare...', 'motus astrorum ignoro', etc.). Terminal semicolon after 'nescio' normalized to a full stop.

question: Quid superest de corporibus? quis membra, quis ossa invenit?
answer: Obtritum volgi perit omne cadaver more animae.
derivation: Umbricius poses these rhetorical questions about a man crushed by a fallen wagon-load and answers them himself. Question spans the two interrogative sentences (lines 259-261); answer is the directly following sentence stating nothing remains - the crushed corpse vanishes like the soul - ending at its full stop after 'animae' (he then moves on to 'domus interea secura...'). Stripped the dangling every-5-lines verse number '260' from mid-span and normalized the first word's capitalization.

question: Quidnam igitur censes? conciditur?
answer: Absit ab illo dedecus hoc, testa alta paretur quae tenui muro spatiosum colligat orbem. Debetur magnus patinae subitusque Prometheus.
derivation: A real interrogative ('quidnam igitur censes? conciditur?' = what then do you advise? is it to be cut up?) is directly answered by Montanus. Dropped the framing tag 'Montanus ait' that interrupts the reply. Answer window begins at the operative response 'absit ab illo dedecus hoc' (the proposal: don't cut it up, prepare a dish) and ends after the contiguous instruction about needing a great Prometheus to make the patina; stopped before the further imperative 'argillam atque rotam citius properate, sed ex hoc tempore iam, Caesar, figuli tua castra sequantur' which turns to elaboration/exhortation. Stripped inline verse numbers 130 and 135.

question: Uis tu consuetis, audax conuiua, canistris impleri panisque tui nouisse colorem?
answer: Scilicet hoc fuerat, propter quod saepe relicta coniuge per montem aduersum gelidasque cucurri Esquilias, fremeret saeua cum grandine uernus Iuppiter et multo stillaret paenula nimbo.
derivation: Direct-speech exchange. A servant taunts the guest with a real interrogative (uis tu...?, 'do you want to be filled from your usual baskets and know the colour of your own bread?'). The guest Trebius answers with a complete bitter retort ('so THIS was the reason I ran...'). Stripped the inline verse number 75 from after 'colorem' and the embedding quotes. The answer ends at the full stop after 'nimbo'; the next line begins a new authorial section ('aspice quam longo...'). Other ?-bearing lines (8-11, 18-19, 62-65, 129-131) are authorial rhetorical questions with no clean answering span, so dropped.

question: Optima sed quare Caesennia teste marito?
answer: Bis quingena dedit.
derivation: A quoted interlocutor's objection ('but why is Caesennia called excellent, her husband being witness?') that Juvenal answers in his own voice. The answer is the first sentence to the first full stop, 'bis quingena dedit' ('she gave 200,000') — the dowry is the reason. Cut before the following sentence 'tanti uocat ille pudicam...', which elaborates rather than answers. First word capitalized, no Latin altered.

question: Cur desiderio Bibulae Sertorius ardet?
answer: Si uerum excutias, facies non uxor amatur.
derivation: A quoted interlocutor's question ('why does Sertorius burn with desire for Bibula?') answered by Juvenal directly: 'if you shake out the truth, the face, not the wife, is loved.' Answer is the complete first sentence to the full stop; the following lines about wrinkles digress. No Latin altered; capitalization normalized.

question: Pone crucem seruo. Meruit quo crimine seruus supplicium? quis testis adest? quis detulit? audi; nulla umquam de morte hominis cunctatio longa est.
answer: Hoc uolo, sic iubeo, sit pro ratione uoluntas.
derivation: Dialogue: the wife commands 'pone crucem seruo' (crucify the slave) — kept as setup so 'seruus' has a referent — and the husband answers with a real interrogative protest ('by what crime did the slave deserve punishment? what witness? who informed?'), quoted contiguously and verbatim. The wife's reply opens with a non-answering preamble of mockery and concession ('o demens, ita seruus homo est? nil fecerit, esto:'), which is skipped; the operative answering sentence is 'hoc uolo, sic iubeo, sit pro ratione uoluntas' ('this I want, so I command, let my will stand for reason') — her answer to 'by what crime/whose testimony'. Quotation marks and speech framing removed; first words capitalized.

question: Quod uocis pretium?
answer: Siccus petasunculus et uas pelamydum aut ueteres, Maurorum epimenia, bulbi aut uinum Tiberi deuectum, quinque lagonae.
derivation: Authorial rhetorical question 'quod uocis pretium?' (what reward for the pleader's voice?) answered immediately and concretely by the catalogue of paltry payment in kind. Inline every-5-lines verse number '120' stripped from after 'bulbi'. Answer runs to the first full stop at 'quinque lagonae.'; what follows ('si quater egisti...') turns to a new conditional and no longer answers the question. First word capitalized; terminal punctuation normalized.

question: Stemmata quid faciunt?
answer: nobilitas sola est atque unica uirtus.
derivation: The satire opens with the author's own rhetorical question 'Stemmata quid faciunt?' (what do family trees accomplish?), line 1. After a long run of further rhetorical questions (quid prodest, quo, cur...) about the uselessness of pedigree, the author states his own resolving thesis at line 20: 'nobilitas sola est atque unica uirtus.' Question and answer are each a single contiguous source sentence; the intervening rhetorical questions are not included in either field. Stripped the inline verse numbers (5, 10, 15, 20) and the bracketed editorial lines.

question: his ego quem monui?
answer: tecum mihi sermo, Rubelli Blande.
derivation: Author poses a genuine interrogative about whom he has been admonishing ('his ego quem monui?', line 39) and immediately answers it himself: 'tecum mihi sermo, Rubelli Blande' (my discourse is with you, Rubellius Blandus). Both fields are verbatim and contiguous across the 39-40 line break; the inline verse number 40 mid-passage is stripped. The answer stops at the full stop; what follows ('tumes alto Drusorum stemmate...') elaborates the rebuke.

question: Iusta doloris, Naeuole, causa tui; contra tamen ille quid adfert?
answer: Neglegit atque alium bipedem sibi quaerit asellum.
derivation: The narrator (validating Naevolus's complaint about his patron) asks what the patron offers in return: 'contra tamen ille quid adfert?' Kept the preceding 'iusta doloris, Naeuole, causa tui;' as verbatim setup so 'ille' has a referent. Naevolus answers directly in the next line: 'neglegit atque alium bipedem sibi quaerit asellum.' Capitalized 'Iusta' (starts a new sentence after the full stop following 'impleuero.') and 'Neglegit' (now sentence-initial). Answer cut at the first full stop after 'asellum'; what follows ('haec soli commissa tibi celare memento...') turns to a new topic (keeping it secret), so it is excluded.

question: Utile consilium modo, sed commune, dedisti. nunc mihi quid suades post damnum temporis et spes deceptas? festinat enim decurrere uelox flosculus angustae miseraeque breuissima uitae portio; dum bibimus, dum serta, unguenta, puellas poscimus, obrepit non intellecta senectus.
answer: Ne trepida, numquam pathicus tibi derit amicus stantibus et saluis his collibus; undique ad illos conuenient et carpentis et nauibus omnes qui digito scalpunt uno caput.
derivation: Naevolus's whole speech is one plea built around the interrogative 'nunc mihi quid suades post damnum temporis et spes deceptas?' ('what do you now advise me?'). Quoted the entire contiguous speech verbatim as the question; stripped the dangling inline verse number '125' from the end of the 'spes' line. The narrator answers in the next turn: 'ne trepida... never will you lack a pathic friend.' Stripped the dangling '130' from the 'amicus' line. Capitalized 'Ne' (sentence-initial). The semicolon after 'collibus' is not a full stop, so the answer continues to the full stop after 'caput'; cut there before 'altera maior spes superest...' (further elaboration).

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum I, sec. 9 (Kalila and Dimna)
question: Quomodo manifestum est tibi quod leo sit in cogitacione?
answer: Cognosco motum ipsius, quia vir intelligens potest cognoscere cogitacionem propinqui, investigans vultum eius et cogitaciones ipsius.
derivation: Kililes asks Dimnes how he can tell the lion is preoccupied; Dimnes answers directly. Stripped speech tags 'Kililes ait' / 'Et Dimnes respondit'. The answer is a single sentence ending at the first full stop; the next line is a new question from Kililes ('Quomodo potest aliquis graciam invenire...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum I, sec. 10 (lion and Dimna)
question: Quis es tu et quid queris et ubi tantum temporis conversatus es?
answer: Cottidie assisto imperialibus ianuis, sperans inde aliquem honorem adipisci, sciens quod multis opus habet imperator. Et oportet quod recipiat magnos et parvos, nam hii multociens iuvant imperium sicut lignum iacens in terra derelictum, magno tamen edificio aliquando necessarium est.
derivation: Lion's three-part question to Dimnes; Dimnes answers who he is and what he seeks. Stripped framing 'Leo vero interrogavit eum' / 'Et Dimnes respondit'; stripped editorial '+' artifact after 'adipisci' and editorial brackets on 'hii'. Answer kept through Dimnes's reply (two sentences) before the narrator resumes ('Audiens leo hunc sermonem...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum I, sec. 15 (bull and Dimna)
question: Quis est iste leo qui te ad me misit et ubi manet?
answer: Imperator est omnium ferarum et in hoc loco cum suo exercitu manet.
derivation: The bull (thaurus) asks who and where the lion is; Dimnes answers both. Stripped speech tags 'Ait thaurus' / 'Respondit Dimnes'. Answer is the full single sentence of the reply before narration resumes ('Thaurus vero timens secutus est eum...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum I, sec. 37 (lion and the crow / camel tale)
question: Quomodo?
answer: Comede camelum qui inter nos conversatur.
derivation: The crow says he can refresh the ailing lion; the lion asks 'Quomodo?' and the crow answers what to do. Setup retained via the preceding clause is unnecessary because 'Quomodo' + answer is self-contained as a how-question. Stripped tags 'Leo dixit' / 'Corvus ait'. Answer is the single-sentence reply before the lion's furious retort ('Et leo furibundus ait...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum III, sec. 77 (mouse and crow)
question: Quis es, amice?
answer: Ego sum corvus et vidi pulcram amiciciam quam ad amicos habes et vellem esse amicus tuus, et propterea veni ad te.
derivation: The mouse asks the unseen caller who he is; the crow identifies himself and his purpose. Stripped tags 'Ipse autem respondit' / 'Et corvus respondit'. Answer kept to the crow's full self-identifying sentence before the mouse's objection ('Mus autem dixit: Quid est commune...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum III, sec. 79 (hermit and stranger / mouse tale)
question: Subsanas me, quia loquor tecum?
answer: Oportet te prius interrogare qua occasione ego plaudo manibus, et dicam tibi: nam in ista domo est mus a quo magnum pacior contrarium, quia comedit annonam meam et corrumpit eam.
derivation: The indignant stranger asks whether the hermit is mocking him by clapping; the hermit explains he claps not in mockery but because of a destructive mouse. Stripped tags 'Extraneus autem indignatus dixit' / 'Heremita respondit'. The reply is a single connected explanation (the colon is internal, not a sentence end); kept whole through the operative answer before the stranger's next question ('Extraneus ait: Unus mus est an multi?').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum IV, sec. 113 (old serpent and frog tale)
question: Quare es in cogitacione?
answer: Quomodo non debeo cogitare, cum semper de hoc gurgite vitam habuerim? Et nunc ivi ad patriam et heremita dixit mihi ut nullam de vobis amplius per vim accipiam et volo de cetero regi vestro esse subiectus.
derivation: A frog asks the brooding serpent why he is lost in thought; the serpent answers (the deceitful pretext that explains his presence). Stripped tags 'dixit' / 'Ipse respondit'. Answer kept through the serpent's full reply before narration resumes ('Rana autem ivit et renunciavit...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum IV, sec. 114 (crow and his king)
question: Quomodo vidisti regem bubonum et conversacionem eorum?
answer: Stultam, malam et anomalam et sine ordine preter illum qui consiliatus est me occidere; ipse enim erat omnibus intelligencior.
derivation: The king of the crows asks the crow how he found the owl-king and his court; the crow answers. Stripped tags 'Rex ait' / 'Et ille ait'. Answer is the full single reply before the king's follow-up question ('Rex dixit: Quid tibi visum est...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum V, sec. 116 (turtle and the monkey)
question: Quis es, amice, qui tales fructus mihi dedisti?
answer: Miser alienigena sum qui propter senectutem meam eiectus sum de regno meo, et nisi fugissem, occisus fuissem.
derivation: The turtle, sweetened by the figs, asks who the monkey is; the monkey identifies himself as an exiled stranger. Stripped tags 'respexit sursum et dixit' / 'Symeus respondit'. Answer cut after the first full stop ('...occisus fuissem.'); the monkey then elaborates ('Et ego qui eram multarum gencium dominus...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum V, sec. 116 (turtle and the monkey)
question: Ergo non habes tecum cor tuum?
answer: Non, quia preceptum habemus in lege nostra ut, cum ad domos amicorum pergimus, domi corda nostra relinquamus, ne forte aliquid adversum contra amicum nostrum cogitemus.
derivation: The turtle, having let slip she needs the monkey's heart, asks in surprise whether he hasn't his heart with him; the monkey (saving himself by a ruse) answers no, with a reason. Stripped tags 'Ait testudo' / 'Respondit symeus'. Answer kept to the monkey's full single reply before narration resumes ('Hec dicens testudo veloci cursu reversa est...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum V, sec. 117 (sick lion, fox, and ass)
question: O rex, qualiter video te ita afflictum?
answer: Propter infirmitatem istam que me occupavit, de qua non potero sanari nisi per cor et auriculas asini.
derivation: The fox asks the sick lion why he is so afflicted; the lion answers, naming the cure he needs. Stripped tags 'Dixit ei vulpis' / 'Respondit leo'. Answer is the lion's full single reply before the fox's offer ('Vulpis dixit: Leve est hoc facere...').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum V, sec. 117 (fox and ass)
question: Quare te video macilentum et plagis plenum?
answer: Malicia patroni mei facit hoc; pondere magno me onerat et parvam mihi tribuit comestionem et tota die me ligatum stare facit.
derivation: The fox asks the ass why he is so emaciated and beaten; the ass answers, blaming his master. Stripped tags 'dixit ei' / 'Respondit asinus'. Answer is the ass's full single reply before the fox's next question ('Vulpis dixit: Quare hec omnia suffers?').

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum V, sec. 117 (lion and fox / the ass's heart)
question: Ubi sunt aures et cor asini?
answer: Si habuisset iste asinus cor ad intelligendum et aures ad audiendum, nunquam ad te reversus fuisset, videns primum periculum unde evaserat.
derivation: The returning lion asks where the ass's ears and heart are; the fox (who has eaten them) wittily answers that the ass plainly had neither, since it came back. Stripped tags 'Reversus leo dixit' / 'Vulpis respondit'. The fox's reply is the final sentence of the tale; nothing follows.

locus: Liber Kalilae et Dimnae, Capitulum X, sec. 135 (lion and the panther/hermit)
question: Quid fecisti de carne?
answer: Dedi eam senescalo tuo.
derivation: The lion, finding the meat gone (planted in the panther's house by enemies), summons the panther and asks what he did with the meat; the panther answers directly. Stripped tags 'dixit ei' / 'Panther dixit'. Answer is the panther's full single reply before the steward is summoned ('Vocatus senescalus...').

locus: Thomas a Kempis, De Imitatione Christi 1.22.1
question: Quis est qui habeat omnia secundum suam voluntatem?
answer: Nec ego, nec tu, nec aliquis hominum super terram.
derivation: Author poses the question and answers it immediately in the next sentence. The question is verbatim from the source; the answer is the full directly-responding sentence (a list of who does NOT have everything as they wish). Stops at the first full stop; what follows ('Nemo est in mundo sine aliqua tribulatione...') generalizes rather than answers.

locus: Thomas a Kempis, De Imitatione Christi 1.22.1
question: Quis est, qui melius habet?
answer: Utique qui pro Deo aliquid pati valet.
derivation: Author asks who is better off and answers it himself with 'Utique...' ('assuredly, the one who...'). Both the interrogative and its single-sentence answer are taken verbatim and contiguously from the source; this is the end of the paragraph, so nothing follows to cut.

question: Unum scilicet, quod sibi summe necessarium est. Quid illud?
answer: Ut omnibus relictis se relinquat, et a se totaliter exeat, nihilque de privato amore retineat.
derivation: Author poses and answers his own question. Kept the preceding 'Unum scilicet, quod sibi summe necessarium est' as setup so that 'illud' has a referent (the one necessary thing). Answer is the immediately following sentence that states what that one thing is; stopped at the first full stop, before the next sentence 'Cum omnia fecerit quae facienda noverit, nihil se fecisse sentiat,' which elaborates rather than answers.

locus: Thomas a Kempis, De Imitatione Christi 3.6.1
question: Fili, non es adhuc fortis et prudens amator. Quare, Domine?
answer: Quia modicam propter contrarietatem deficis, accipis et nimis avide consolationem quaeris.
derivation: The Lord states 'Fili, non es adhuc fortis et prudens amator' (kept verbatim as setup so 'Quare' has a referent), the soul asks the genuine interrogative 'Quare, Domine?', and the Lord answers with 'Quia...'. Answer cut at the first full stop after 'quaeris'; what follows ('Fortis amator stat in tentationibus...') is elaboration, not the direct reply. Dropped the leading section-number scaffold '1.'.

locus: Thomas a Kempis, De Imitatione Christi 3.11.1
question: Fili, oportet te adhuc multa discere, quae necdum bene didicisti. Quae sunt haec, Domine?
answer: Ut desiderium tuum ponas totaliter secundum beneplacitum meum, et tui ipsius amator non sis: sed meae voluntatis cupidus amator et aemulator.
derivation: The Lord's sentence 'oportet te adhuc multa discere, quae necdum bene didicisti' is kept verbatim as setup so 'haec' has a referent; the soul asks the real interrogative 'Quae sunt haec, Domine?', and the Lord answers 'ut desiderium tuum ponas...'. Answer cut at the first full stop after 'aemulator'; what follows ('Desideria te saepe accendunt...') is further exhortation. Dropped the leading section-number scaffold '1.'.

locus: Thomas a Kempis, De Imitatione Christi 3.12.2
question: An putas quod homines saeculi huius nihil, aut parum patiantur?
answer: Nec hoc invenies, etiamsi delicatissimos quaesieris.
derivation: The Lord poses a genuine interrogative ('An putas quod...?') and immediately answers it himself ('Nec hoc invenies, etiamsi delicatissimos quaesieris'). Answer is a single sentence to its full stop; what follows ('Sed habent, inquies, multas delectationes...') is an anticipated objection, not the answer. Self-contained without prior context.

locus: Thomas a Kempis, De Imitatione Christi 3.25.2-3
question: Neque tunc magni aliquid te reputes aut specialiter dilectum existimes, si in magna fueris devotione aut dulcedine: quia in istis non cognoscitur verus amator virtutis, nec in istis consistit profectus, et perfectio hominis. In quo ergo, Domine?
answer: In offerendo te ex toto corde tuo voluntati divinae, non quaerendo quae tua sunt, nec in parvo nec in magno, nec in tempore nec in aeternitate, ita ut una aequali facie in gratiarum actione permaneas inter prospera et contraria omnia aequa lance pensando.
derivation: The Lord's final sentence of section 2 ('...nec in istis consistit profectus, et perfectio hominis') is kept verbatim as setup so the soul's interrogative 'In quo ergo, Domine?' has a referent (in what does the profectus consist). The Lord answers 'In offerendo te ex toto corde...'. Answer cut at the first full stop after 'pensando'; what follows ('Si fueris tam fortis...') is conditional elaboration. Dropped the section-number scaffold '3.' between the two speaker turns.

locus: Thomas a Kempis, De Imitatione Christi 3.37.2-3
question: Domine, quoties me resignabo? et in quibus me relinquam?
answer: Semper et in omni hora: sicut in parvo, sic et in magno.
derivation: The soul asks two direct interrogatives ('quoties me resignabo? et in quibus me relinquam?'), and the Lord answers 'Semper et in omni hora: sicut in parvo, sic et in magno.'. Answer cut at the first full stop after 'magno'; what follows ('Nihil excipio...') elaborates. Dropped the leading section-number scaffolds '2.' and '3.'.

locus: Kepler, Strena seu de nive sexangula (ed. Frankfurt 1611)
question: Nix quid sit?
answer: Nihil.
derivation: Author frames an embedded question and its answer: 'Nam si Germano quaeras, nix quid sit, respondebit Nihil, siquidem Latine possit.' Dropped the speech framing 'Nam si Germano quaeras' (the asking) and 'respondebit ... siquidem Latine possit' (the answering tag and its proviso), leaving the bare interrogative 'nix quid sit' (normalized capitalization and terminal '?') and the answer 'Nihil'.

locus: Kepler, Strena seu de nive sexangula (ed. Frankfurt 1611)
question: Quaeras, unde hoc sciam, cum, si talis etiam sit vapor, id oculis cerni non possit, quia vapor pellucidus?
answer: Vapor existit ex resolutione humoris subterranei, quod arguitur ex ejus levitate et ascensu.
derivation: Author poses a question to himself and answers with 'Respondeo:'. Kept the full interrogative sentence as the question (it is contiguous and self-contained). Dropped the framing tag 'Respondeo:' from the answer; took the answer's first sentence (to the first full stop), which genuinely answers how he knows the vapor is undifferentiated. Cut before 'In resolutione vero figurae non habent locum...' which begins elaboration.

locus: Kepler, Strena seu de nive sexangula (ed. Frankfurt 1611)
question: Quo ordine structi sint apum alveoli?
answer: Ordine sexangulo.
derivation: From 'Si ex geometris quaeras, quo ordine structi sint apum alveoli, respondebunt, ordine sexangulo.' Dropped the speech framing 'Si ex geometris quaeras' (the asking) and 'respondebunt' (the answering tag), leaving the bare embedded interrogative 'quo ordine structi sint apum alveoli' (normalized capitalization and terminal '?') and its direct answer 'ordine sexangulo' (normalized capitalization and terminal '.'). Cut before 'Simplex est responsio...' which begins explanation rather than the answer itself.

question: Quid frater eius Maximianus, qui est dictus Herculius?
answer: Non dissimilis ab eo.
derivation: Authorial rhetorical question that the author immediately answers himself. Question is the full interrogative sentence. The answer is the operative reply 'Non dissimilis ab eo'; cut at the colon in the source ('Non dissimilis ab eo:'), terminal colon normalized to a period, before the explanatory continuation 'nec enim possent in amicitiam...'.

question: Quid opus est consilio, cum sit necesse illis duobus placere quicquid nos fecimur?
answer: Ita plane. Nam illorum filios nuncupari necesse est.
derivation: Direct-speech exchange between Galerius (asking) and Diocletian (answering) over choosing the Caesars. Question and answer are quoted verbatim from the source ('"Quid opus est consilio..."--"Ita plane. Nam illorum filios nuncupari necesse est."'). Nothing cut; the answer ends at its natural full stop before the next quoted line.

question: Quos ergo faciemus?
answer: Severum.
derivation: Direct-speech exchange: Diocletian asks whom they shall make Caesars, Galerius answers 'Severum'. Speech tag 'inquit' (source: '"Severum" inquit') dropped as framing; answer is the single naming word, terminal punctuation normalized.

question: Quis est hic quem mihi offers?
answer: Meus affinis.
derivation: Direct-speech exchange: Diocletian asks who the second nominee (Daia) is, Galerius answers 'Meus affinis'. Source ('Quis est hic quem mihi offers?"--"Meus" inquit "affinis."') lacks an opening quote mark on the question (scaffolding noise) and splits the answer around the speech tag 'inquit'; tag dropped as framing, answer rejoined contiguously as the speaker's own two words in source order.

question: Si Deus unus est, quae esse beata solitudo queat?
answer: Tamquam nos, qui unum esse dicimus, desertum ac solitarium esse dicamus; habet enim ministros, quos uocamus nuntios.
derivation: Lactantius cites the objection of Hortensius (in Cicero) and answers it himself. Dropped the framing 'Sed fortasse quaerat aliquis a nobis idem illud, quod apud Ciceronem quaerit Hortensius:' which narrates the asking. The reply rebuts the premise ('as if we... say he is solitary') and gives the operative answer 'habet enim ministros'; window ends at the first full stop after 'nuntios'. What follows ('Et est illud uerum, quod dixisse in Exhortationibus Senecam...') is supporting elaboration.

question: Quomodo ergo dii crediti sunt?
answer: Nimirum quia reges maximi ac potentissimi fuerint: ob merita uirtutum suarum, aut munerum, aut artium repertarum, cum cari fuissent iis quibus imperitauerant, in memoriam sunt consecrati.
derivation: An imagined interlocutor asks how mortals came to be believed gods; Lactantius answers. Dropped the interior speech tag 'inquiet aliquis,' from 'Quomodo ergo, inquiet aliquis, dii crediti sunt?', keeping the author's own words contiguous. Answer runs to the first full stop after 'consecrati'; what follows ('Quod is quis dubitet, res eorum gestas...') turns to corroboration.

question: Quid tu poetisne credendum putas?
answer: Quidni putem?
derivation: An imagined interlocutor asks whether the poets should be believed; Lactantius answers affirmatively. Dropped the interior speech tag 'inquiet aliquis,' from 'Quid tu, inquiet aliquis, poetisne credendum putas?', keeping the utterance contiguous. The answer is the single retort 'Quidni putem?'; what follows ('Non enim ista Lucilius narrat...') is justification.

locus: Landor, Latina Quaedam (1858), "Qualis Vita Sit Beata"
question: Quae sit vita beata?
answer: Brevis.
derivation: The poem ends 'Iamque rogas quae sit vita beata? Brevis.' Dropped the framing 'Iamque rogas' ('and now you ask') as narration of the asking; the operative interrogative is 'quae sit vita beata?', answered by the single word 'Brevis.' The preceding 'Multos perdidimus, paucos retinemus amicos' is context but not needed for the question to be intelligible, so it is left out.

question: Rege Borussorum quis turpior?
answer: Ecce Borussos Ipsos!
derivation: Genuine direct interrogative 'Rege Borussorum quis turpior?' immediately answered 'Ecce Borussos Ipsos!'. Answer window ends at the exclamation; what follows ('perfidiam non renuêre pati') elaborates rather than answers, so it is cut.

question: Vis alios digito monstrem tibi?
answer: Respice Gallos.
derivation: Genuine yes/no interrogative 'Vis alios digito monstrem tibi?' answered by the directive 'Respice Gallos'. The terminal comma after 'Gallos' is normalized to a full stop; what follows ('Omnia quos pariter, praeter honesta, iuvant') elaborates and is cut.

locus: Landor, Poematum Latinorum Libellus, Hendecasyllabi XXV
question: Quid prohibet fortes cantu celebrare Britannos, cum mihi sint vires?
answer: Vellem equidem fortes cantu celebrare Britannos, et licet, at fidos non celebrare licet.
derivation: The friend's question is explicitly marked as asked by the speech-frame 'dulcis Amice! rogas' at the end of the second line; that frame is narration of the asking and is dropped, leaving the real interrogative 'Quid prohibet... cum mihi sint vires?'. The poet's reply opens with the answering couplet 'Vellem equidem... non celebrare licet.' which directly answers (he would wish to and may, but is not permitted to celebrate the disloyal); the answer window ends at the first full stop. The following lines 'Si facerem certe gelidus tacitusque iacebo...' elaborate on the consequences and are cut. Table-scaffolding (column borders, the 'XXV' poem marker) and verse line indentation were stripped.

question: Et quis est ille deus, qui concumbet mecum?
answer: Ille est Ammon, qui largitur divicias in omnibus.
derivation: Olimpiadis asks which god will lie with her; Nectanebus answers naming Ammon. Dropped the speech tags 'At ille dixit' (question) and 'Nectanebus inquit' (answer). Answer is the full single-sentence reply.

question: Et quam figuram habet?
answer: Neque iuvenis neque vetulus, sed in media aetate consistit habens in fronte cornua arietina, canos barbamque ornatam.
derivation: Olimpiadis asks what form the god has; Nectanebus describes him. Dropped tags 'Dixitque illa' and 'Cui ille'. Answer ends at the first full stop (after 'ornatam'); the following sentence 'Unde si tibi placet...' turns from describing to advising and is cut. Stripped editorial brackets around 'arietina', keeping the word.

question: Pater, hae stellae, quas tu computas, parent in caelo?
answer: Etiam, fili.
derivation: Alexander asks Nectanebus whether the stars he computes appear in the sky; Nectanebus affirms. Dropped tags 'dixit' and 'Cui Nectanebus'.

question: Et quam mortem debes facere?
answer: A filio meo moriar.
derivation: Alexander asks Nectanebus what death he will die; Nectanebus answers he will die at the hand of his son. Dropped the framing 'Cui dixit'.

question: Dic mihi, quis es tu?
answer: Ego sum Alexander, filius Philippi.
derivation: Nicolaus asks Alexander who he is; Alexander identifies himself. Dropped speaker frames 'dixit' and 'Cui ille'.

question: Cuius est hec statua?
answer: Statua haec Nectanebi, regis Egiptiorum, est.
derivation: Alexander asks whose statue it is; the Egyptians answer it is the statue of Nectanebus. Dropped 'dixit' and 'At illi dixerunt'.

question: O beatissime et pulcherrime certator, ut quid sine civitate?
answer: Magnissime imperator, antequam tu esses, habui civitatem, nunc autem per te civitatem non habeo.
derivation: Alexander asks Clitomachus why he calls himself 'cityless' (Sinecivitas); Clitomachus answers he had a city before Alexander but now has none because of him. Dropped the tags 'et dixit' and 'Clitomachus dixit'.

question: Quis ex vobis exiet luctans in ludo isto?
answer: Si placet vestrae potestati, ego recepta potestate pugnandi pugnabo et vinco.
derivation: At the Corinthian games Alexander asks who will come out to wrestle; Clitomachus volunteers. Dropped frames 'dixit Alexander' and 'Cui Clitomachus dixit'.

question: Ego debeo accipere ab illo similitudinem?
answer: Alexander in omnibus peritissimus est et in nullo offendit, omnia ipse faciens viriliter; formam et virtutem secundum suam nativitatem leonis habet.
derivation: Darius asks whether he should take an example from Alexander; the satrap (Cui alius satrapas dixit) answers describing Alexander's excellence and lion-like nature. Dropped the speech tag 'Cui alius satrapas dixit'. Answer ends at the full stop after 'leonis habet'; what follows is Darius's next question 'Unde tibi hoc cognitum?', a new exchange.

question: Unde tibi hoc cognitum?
answer: Quando perrexi per tuam iussionem Macedoniam tollere censum Philippo patri suo, vidi eum et cognovi sapientiam illius et figuram eius intellexi.
derivation: Darius asks how the satrap knows this; the satrap (Cui ille) answers that he saw Alexander when sent to collect tribute from Philip. Dropped speech tag 'Cui ille'. Answer ends at first full stop ('intellexi'); what follows ('Quod si tibi placet, congrega omnes satrapas...') turns to advice, not an answer.

question: O strenue vir, quid est hoc?
answer: Ne estimes me, dominator, Macedonam esse, sed Persarum. Et ego promisi Dario venire, aufferre caput tuum; spopondit enim mihi dare in coniugio filiam suam et regales provintias.
derivation: Alexander asks the captured Persian assassin what this is; the Persian (Cui Persa barbarus dixit) answers explaining he is Persian and was sent by Darius to take Alexander's head. Dropped speech tag 'Cui Persa barbarus dixit'. Answer runs to end of his utterance; what follows is narration ('Tunc Alexander iussit...').

question: Quis es tu?
answer: Apochrisarius sum regis Alexandri missus ad te, dicens tibi, quia: moram facit exire preliari in campo cum inimicis suis; timidus est atque pavidus.
derivation: Darius asks the disguised Alexander who he is; Alexander (Cui ille) answers that he is the envoy of king Alexander. Dropped speech tag 'Cui ille'. Answer ends at 'pavidus'; what follows ('Unde si tibi placet, constitue diem preliandi') is a request, not part of the identification. Chose the Darius exchange (clear single asker/answerer) over the earlier corrupt '[Quis es tu?]' bracketed by the Persians at the gate.

question: O fortissime vir, quid est hoc, quod agis? Quare abscondis vasa aurea in sinu tuo?
answer: Noster senior sedens in convivio donat militibus suis vascula, cum quibus bibunt.
derivation: Darius asks why Alexander is hiding the golden cups; Alexander (Cui Alexander) answers that their lord gives soldiers the cups they drink with. Dropped speech tag 'Erexit se Darius et dixit' (narration of the asking) and 'Cui Alexander'. Answer ends at full stop ('bibunt'); what follows is narration of the guests' reaction.

question: Non sunt sepulcra vobis?
answer: Hic, ubi habito, sufficit mihi.
derivation: Alexander asks a gymnosophist a direct interrogative; answer is the man's full reply. Dropped narration 'Alexander vero interrogavit unum ex illis' before and 'Ostendit ei(s) habitationem suam dicens' between. Answer ends at its only sentence.

question: Et si mortalis es, quare vadis discurrendo et faciendo tanta ac talia?
answer: Istae causae non gubernantur nisi de superna providentia; ministri eius sumus facientes iussionem illius.
derivation: The gymnosophists' interrogative answered by Alexander. Setup retained verbatim ('Et si mortalis es' refers to his prior 'Mortalis cum sim'). Answer window taken to first full stop; cut before 'Mare nullomodo turbatur...' where he turns to elaborating analogies. Editorial brackets stripped: Ist[a]e caus[a]e -> Istae causae.

question: Quis es tu?
answer: Filius Candacis reginae sum.
derivation: Ptolemy questions captured Candaulis; direct answer. Dropped speech tags 'Cui Ptolomeus' and 'Et ille'. Editorial brackets stripped: regin[a]e -> reginae.

question: Quare huc venisti?
answer: Exivi cum uxore mea exercere me cum paucis equitibus.
derivation: Ptolemy's interrogative; Candaulis answers. Dropped speech tag 'At ille'. Answer cut at first full stop; what follows ('Rex Bebrecorum sciendo...') narrates the subsequent abduction, beyond the direct answer to 'why did you come here'.

question: Quare mutata est facies tua, quia vocavi te Alexandrum?
answer: Domina, Antigonus nomen est mihi, non Alexander.
derivation: Queen Candacis asks why Alexander's face changed; he answers (falsely) with his alias. Dropped speech tags 'Cui illa' and 'Cui ille'. Single-sentence answer.

question: Si habuisses gladium, quid facere potueras?
answer: Quia traditus sum per meam voluntatem, primum occidam te, postea memet ipsum.
derivation: Candacis' interrogative answered by Alexander. Dropped tags 'Dixit et illa' and 'Et Alexander'. Single-sentence answer.

question: Quis es tu, domine?
answer: Ego sum Sesonchosis, regnum mundi tenens et mundum subiugans, faciens omnes subiectos.
derivation: In the crypt Alexander asks a luminous figure who he is; the figure answers. Dropped tags 'Et ego' and 'Et ille'. Answer cut at first full stop; what follows ('Nomen autem mihi non est...') elaborates beyond the identification.

question: Dic mihi, quod signum est hoc?
answer: O rex, appropinquabit tempus tuum, ut exeas de hoc seculo.
derivation: Alexander asks the soothsayer the meaning of the monstrous birth; the soothsayer answers. Dropped tags 'dicens illi' and 'Suspirans dixit'. Single-sentence answer.

question: Si facturus fueris rex in regno Alexandri, quid mihi bene facturus es?
answer: Facio.
derivation: Perdiccas asks Ptolemy what reward he will give; Ptolemy answers 'Facio'. Dropped tags 'Abiit et dixit ei' and 'At ille dixit', and the trailing narration 'dans illi sacramentum'. Normalized the now-dangling comma to a full stop.

question: Cur non comedis fructum istius arboris?
answer: Deus id prohibuit. Si tetigerimus illum, moriemur.
derivation: Serpent's interrogative to the woman; speech tag 'dixit mulieri' dropped. Answer is the woman's reply via 'Mulier respondit:'; the tag is cut and both reply sentences kept (they explain why she does not eat). Stops before the serpent's next speech 'Minime, inquit serpens...'.

question: Cur times nisi quia comedisti fructum vetitum?
answer: Mulier, quam dedisti mihi sociam, porrexit mihi fructum istum, ut ederem.
derivation: God's question; the interjected framing 'inquit Deus,' is dropped, leaving 'Cur times nisi quia...' contiguous. Answer from 'Adamus respondit:' with the tag cut; one sentence to the full stop. Stops before 'Dominus dixit mulieri:'.

question: Ubi est tuus frater?
answer: Nescio; num ego sum custos fratris mei?
derivation: God's question 'Deus dixit Caino: ubi est tuus frater?'; speech tag dropped. Answer via 'Cainus respondit:' with tag cut; Cain's evasive reply genuinely answers. End of the exchange/section.

question: Mi pater, ecce ligna; sed ubinam est hostia immolanda?
answer: Deus sibi providebit hostiam, fili mi.
derivation: Isaac's interrogative to his father; the framing 'Isaacus dixit patri:' dropped. The vocative setup 'mi pater, ecce ligna' is kept verbatim so the question is intelligible. Answer from 'Cui Abrahamus: Deus, inquit, sibi providebit...'; the framing 'Cui Abrahamus:' and interjected 'inquit,' are dropped, leaving the utterance contiguous.

question: Quis est ille vir?
answer: Ipse est herus meus.
derivation: Rebecca's question 'interrogavit Eliezerem: quis est ille vir?'; narration dropped. Answer via 'Eliezer respondit:' with tag cut. Stops before 'Illa statim operuit se pallio.'

question: Quisnam es tu?
answer: Ego sum Esaus primogenitus tuus; feci quod iussisti, pater; surge, et comede de venatione mea.
derivation: Isaac's question 'Cui Isaacus dixit: quisnam es tu?'; framing dropped. Answer from 'Iacobus respondit:' with tag cut; kept to the full stop (the contiguous reply identifying himself and urging Isaac to eat). Stops before 'Quomodo, ait Isaacus...'.

question: Quomodo potuisti invenire tam cito?
answer: Inveni, pater; Deus ita voluit.
derivation: Isaac's question; the interjected framing 'ait Isaacus,' is dropped, leaving 'Quomodo potuisti invenire tam cito?' contiguous. Answer is the unframed reply 'Inveni, pater; Deus ita voluit.' Stops before 'Isaacus rursum:'.

question: Fratres, unde estis?
answer: Ex urbe Haran.
derivation: Jacob's question 'dixit pastoribus: fratres, unde estis?'; narration dropped. Answer via 'Qui responderunt:' with tag cut. Stops before the next question.

question: Nostisne Labanum?
answer: Novimus.
derivation: Jacob's question 'Quos interrogavit iterum: nostisne Labanum?'; narration dropped. Answer via 'Dixerunt: novimus.' with tag cut. The garbled '‚ Valetne? ‚' exchange that follows (scaffolding-corrupted punctuation) is left out.

question: Salvusne est senex ille quem vos patrem habetis? Vivitne adhuc?
answer: Salvus est pater noster; adhuc vivit.
derivation: Joseph's two interrogatives 'interrogavitque: salvusne est... Vivitne adhuc?'; the framing verb dropped. Answer via 'Qui responderunt:' with tag cut. Stops before 'Iosephus autem, conjectis...'.

locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Lucius Tarquinius Priscus (Accius Navius)
question: Atqui hoc agitabam an cotem illam secare novacula possem.
answer: Potes ergo.
derivation: The king tests the augur's claim that what he is silently thinking can be done. Stripped the speech tags 'inquit rex' and 'inquit augur'; the narrative 'et secuisse dicitur' follows and is omitted. The king's words contain the indirect interrogative 'an ... possem' (whether he could cut the whetstone); 'Potes ergo' genuinely answers it (you can).

locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Publius Valerius Laevinus (Cineas and Pyrrhus)
question: Superatis Romanis, quid agere destinas, O rex?
answer: Italiae vicina est Sicilia, nec difficile erit eam armis occupare.
derivation: First exchange of the Cineas/Pyrrhus dialogue chain. Took only the first Q&A pair (clean and self-contained); dropped the speech tags 'respondit Cineas' (already absent here) and 'inquit Pyrrhus' from the answer. The later questions ('Occupata Sicilia, quid postea acturus es?', 'Quid deinde?', 'Quin tu isto otio jam nunc frueris?') are separate exchanges, not joined.

locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Aulus Atilius Calatinus (Calpurnius)
question: Fidum quidem et providum hoc consilium videtur; sed quisnam erit qui ducat quadringentos illos milites ad eum locum?
answer: Si alium neminem reperis, me ad hoc consilium perficiendum uti potes. Ego hanc tibi et reipublicae animam do.
derivation: Quoted the consul's full reply as the question (whole-utterance preserved): it accepts the plan then asks who will lead the 400 men. Calpurnius answers that he himself will. Stripped 'Respondit consul:' and the inline 'inquit Calpurnius'. Kept both answer sentences as a contiguous span.

locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Publius Cornelius Scipio Africanus (Scipio and Hannibal)
question: Quidnam igitur tu diceres, si me vicisses?
answer: Me vero et ante Alexandrum et ante Pyrrhum et ante alios omnes posuissem.
derivation: Final, direct-speech turn of the Scipio/Hannibal ranking-of-generals exchange (the earlier turns are reported indirectly, so dropped). Stripped the tags 'Tum ridens Scipio:' / 'inquit' and 'respondit Annibal'. Hannibal's reply genuinely answers the hypothetical.

locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Publius Scipio Nasica (Nasica the censor)
question: Quidnam causae est cur sis tu, quam equus pinguior?
answer: Quoniam ego me ipse curo, equum vero servus.
derivation: Census-review exchange. Stripped 'inquit censor' and 'respondit eques'. The eques genuinely answers why he is fatter than his horse (he tends himself, a slave tends the horse). Following narration 'Minus verecundum visum est responsum...' omitted.

locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Lucius Paulus Aemilius Macedonicus (Paulus and Tertia)
question: Quid est, mea Tertia, quid tristis es?
answer: Mi pater, Perse periit.
derivation: Father asks his little daughter why she is sad; she answers that Perse (her puppy) has died. Stripped the tags 'inquit' and 'inquit illa'. The parenthetical gloss '(Erat autem mortua catella eo nomine)' and the reply 'Accipio omen' are narration/next-turn and omitted; the answer genuinely answers the question.

locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Tiberius Gracchus et Caius Gracchus (Gracchus and Piso)
question: Qui tibi constas, Piso, cum ea lege frumentum petas quam dissuasisti?
answer: Nolim quidem, Grache, mea bona tibi viritim dividere liceat: sed si facias, partem petam.
derivation: Gracchus challenges Piso for taking grain under a law Piso opposed; Piso answers. Stripped 'eum sic compellavit...' (framing) and 'Cui Piso:' / 'inquit'. The question is self-contained ('ea lege ... quam dissuasisti' identifies the grain law).

locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Tiberius Gracchus et Caius Gracchus (the consul and Blosius)
