The veterans' shout 'quo... habemus?' is a real interrogative (quo = to what end), answered directly by Constantine declaring he intends to increase, not diminish, their wellbeing; answer ends at its first full stop. Dropped the later exchange 'quae sunt maxime munera... gravant?' / 'ipse perspicis scilicet.' because the reply evades rather than answers (no actual burdens named); and dropped Victorinus's plea 'muneribus et oneribus... non sinamur' as a statement, not a question.

locus: Johannes de Alta Silva, De thesauro et fure astuto (father's speech)
question: Quid ergo tibi magis faciam?
answer: Hoc tantum unum superest consilii, sed periculosum, ut si ea largitate qua prius vivere vis, turrim in qua regis positi sunt thesauri sub obscurae noctis silentio adeamus.
derivation: The father poses the interrogative 'Quid ergo tibi magis faciam?' within his own speech and answers it himself. I cut the preamble 'Doleo quidem quod fama nomenque tuum in flore iuventutis deperit, sed unde te sustentem non habeo.' which laments but does not answer (per skip-non-answering-preamble), and start the answer at the operative sentence 'Hoc tantum unum superest consilii...'. The answer ends at its first full stop (before 'Audito hoc filius: ...'). Speech tag 'inquit' and the surrounding narration are dropped as framing.

locus: Thomas Edessenus, Tractatus de Nativitate, Caput III
question: Item Angelus, cum revelatus est pastoribus eisque nuntiavit, non praedicabat eis Dominum nostrum ex virgine natum. Quid enim dicebat eis?
answer: Annuntio vobis quidem gaudium magnum quod erit universo mundo.
derivation: Authorial-rhetorical: the author asks what the angel said and answers with the angel's quoted words. Setup sentence (Item Angelus... ex virgine natum) kept verbatim so 'dicebat eis' has its subject and referent. Answer is the quoted utterance, stripped of the framing guillemets; it stops at its full stop before the next question 'Et cur dicit:'.

locus: Thomas Edessenus, Tractatus de Nativitate, Caput III
question: Et cur dicit: Hodie quidem natus est vobis Salvator, qui est Dominus Christus, in civitato David?
answer: Facit mentionem civitatis David, ut ostendat quod in eo qui hodie natus est, impletae sunt Dei promissiones ad patres.
derivation: Authorial-rhetorical: author asks why the angel says the quoted phrase, then answers. Question keeps the embedded scriptural quotation (verbatim, including 'civitato'); guillemets stripped. Answer cut at the first full stop; what follows ('et quod in eo benedicentur omnes populi...') elaborates with further scriptural promises and is omitted.

locus: Thomas Edessenus, Tractatus de Nativitate, Caput VI
question: Veritas enim et gratia per Iesum Christum fuit. Cur 'veritas et gratia' dixit?
answer: Quia Deum nemo vidit unquam.
derivation: Authorial-rhetorical: author quotes John, asks why John used 'veritas et gratia', and answers. The Johannine quotation is kept verbatim as setup so 'dixit' has its referent; the framing tag 'dioit Ioannes' (a narration of speaking) is dropped, guillemets stripped. Answer is the single causal sentence directly answering; what follows (another scriptural quotation about God dwelling in light) is new material and omitted.

question: Delos ubi nunc, Phoebe, tua est, ubi Delphica Pytho?
answer: Nempe Amor in parua te iubet esse casa.
derivation: Self-contained authorial-rhetorical question and answer occupying one couplet. The poet asks where Apollo's sacred sites (Delos, Delphic Pytho) are now, and answers in the next line that Love compels him into a humble hut (continuing the preceding passage on Apollo's servitude to Admetus for love). Question is both interrogative clauses of line 153 (ending at the question mark). Answer is the full pentameter line 154 (to the full stop); nothing cut. Capitalized first word and added terminal period normalized; what follows is a new thought beginning 'felices olim'.

question: Vera quidem moneo, sed prosunt quid mihi uera?
answer: Illius est nobis lege colendus amor.
derivation: Authorial-rhetorical pair within one couplet. The setup clause 'uera quidem moneo' is kept as verbatim source text so that 'uera' in the interrogative has its referent (Rule 2, self-contained); the interrogative is 'sed prosunt quid mihi uera?'. The answer (line 262, full pentameter to the full stop) explains why truth is useless to him: love must be cultivated on her terms. First word capitalization normalized; what follows is a new thought 'quin etiam sedes iubeat...'.

question: Summe sator, cui nostra dies volventibus annis tot peragit reficitque vices, tuane ista voluntas Graiaque nunc undis duce te nutuque secundo it ratis? an meritos fas est mihi rumpere questus? hoc metuens et nequa foret manus invida nato non mediae telluris opes, non improba legi divitis arva plagae (teneant uberrima Teucer et Libys et vestri Pelopis domus): horrida saevo quae premis arva gelu strictosque insedimus amnes. cederet his etiam et sese sine honore referret ulterius, sed nube rigens ac nescia rerum stat super et nostros iam zona reverberat ignes. quid regio immanis, quid barbarus amnibus ullis Phasis et aversis proles mea gentibus obstat? quid Minyae meruere queri? num vellere Graio vi potitur? profugo quin agmina iungere Phrixo abnuit, Inoas ultor nec venit ad aras, imperii sed parte virum nataeque moratus coniugio videt e Graia nunc stirpe nepotes et generos vocat et iunctas sibi sanguine terras. flecte ratem motusque, pater, nec vulnere nostro aequora pande viris; veteris sat conscia luctus silva Padi et viso flentes genitore sorores!
answer: Vetera haec nobis et condita pergunt ordine cuncta suo rerumque a principe cursu fixa manent.
derivation: Sol's entire speech to Jupiter (1.507-529, bounded by the quotation marks after the speech tag 'tales fundit Sol pectore voces:') is quoted verbatim and contiguous as the question; it contains genuine interrogatives (tuane ista voluntas... it ratis? an... fas est? quid regio... obstat? quid Minyae meruere queri? num vellere Graio vi potitur?) and the closing plea 'flecte ratem'. The author's parenthetical (teneant... domus) is part of the utterance and kept. The narration at 530-532 (adfremit his... Saturnia questus) is dropped as framing. For the answer I take Jupiter's reply (introduced by the framing tag 'Tum genitor:'), whose operative first sentence directly answers whether this is his will: 'vetera haec nobis et condita pergunt ordine cuncta suo rerumque a principe cursu fixa manent' (these things are ancient and fixed from the origin). The window ends at the first full stop ('fixa manent;', 1.535); what follows ('neque enim terris tum sanguis...') elaborates the reasoning. No editorial <...> brackets or scaffolding occur in either span.

question: Quod, virgo, tibi nomenque genusque, quae sors ista, doce, tendunt cur vincula palmas?
answer: Nos Ili felix quondam genus, invida donec Laomedonteos fugeret fortuna penates.
derivation: Hercules (ductor ait) asks the chained virgin Hesione her name, lineage (genus), fate (sors), and why she is bound; question taken verbatim, dropping the speech tag 'ductor ait'. Her reply opens with the non-answering deflection 'non ego digna malis. suprema parentum / dona vides ostro scopulos auroque frequentes.' which laments rather than answers; the answer window advances to the operative sentence stating her lineage ('nos Ili felix quondam genus... penates'), which answers the genus/origin question. Cut stops at 'penates.' (first full stop of the answering sentence); what follows ('principio morbi...') digresses into the plague and sea-monster narrative.

question: Bebryxne venis diversaque regi corda gerens--melior vulgi nam saepe voluntas--hostis an externis fato delatus ab oris? et tua cur Amycus caestu nondum obruit ora?
answer: Me numquam leto dignatus et armis, sed lacrimis potius luctuque absumor inerti.
derivation: Direct speech: the ductor (Jason) asks the mourning youth two interrogatives (whether he is a Bebryx/foreigner, and why Amycus has not yet crushed his face). Stripped the speech tag 'ductor ad haec:' before the question and 'ait' after the answer's first word. The reply opens with a textually corrupt, non-answering preamble narrating his name and origin ('nomen ait praedulce mihi ~nomen~que secutus Otreos unanimi... ego palmas implicui'), which contains crux markers (~...~) and does not answer; per answer-window guidance the start is advanced to the operative answering sentence 'me numquam leto dignatus et armis, sed lacrimis potius luctuque absumor inerti', which directly answers 'cur... nondum obruit' (Amycus never deemed him worthy of death). Window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('spes tamen, his fando si nuntius extitit oris...') digresses to his hopes of rescue.

question: Magna pariter quos mole petamus? cernis, Colchos habeant quae proelia quique nunc status. hinc Perses, illinc non viribus aequis apparat Aeetes aciem. quibus addimur armis?
answer: Stat pectore fixum Aeetae sociare manus.
derivation: Pallas (virgo) asks Iuno which side to support; speech tag 'ait' dropped from the question, leaving the utterance contiguous (cernis...Colchos are adjacent in source once 'ait' is removed). Iuno's reply opens with the non-answering preamble 'dimitte metus, ne proelia forte hinc tibi grata negem' (plus an editorial gap '< . . . >' and a digression about her sweat/horses) which does not answer 'whose arms'; advanced the answer's start to the operative sentence 'stat pectore fixum Aeetae sociare manus.' (cut ends there at the full stop; what follows is 'scio perfida regis corda...' elaboration).

question: Quae manus haec, certo ceu me petat agmine, mater, advenit haud armis, haud umquam cognita cultu?
answer: Non tibi ab hoste minae nec vis ulla propinquat nec metus: externo iam flammea murice cerno tegmina, iam vittas frondemque imbellis olivae. Graius adest, Graio sic cuncta simillima Phrixo.
derivation: Medea asks her nurse what band approaches; trailing non-question sentence 'quaere fugam, precor, et tutos circumspice saltus' omitted from the question as it is an imperative plea, not the interrogative. Nurse Henioche answers; speech tag 'ait' dropped, editorial bracket '[te]' stripped keeping no extra words. Answer kept through 'Graius adest...Phrixo.' which directly identifies the approaching men as Greeks.

question: O Iovis alma progenies, an patriam spes ulla videndi?
answer: Nec ferus Aeetes, ut fama, nec aurea nobis terga negat, bello interea sed pressus iniquo auxilium petit.
derivation: The Minyae ask Castor whether there is any hope of seeing home; the bracketing imperatives 'fare ... fare' (framing of the asking) dropped, leaving the contiguous interrogative 'o Iovis alma progenies, an patriam spes ulla videndi'. Castor's framing 'ille in mediis sic orsus Achivis' precedes; answer taken to the first full stop 'auxilium petit.' which answers the hope question (Aeetes does not refuse; cut before the following 'armatos dux...' logistical detail).

question: Quis procul ille virum nobis, quem balteus asper subligat et stricto stat proximus armiger arcu ceu pugnam paret et positas confundere mensas?
answer: Quem rogitas, Carmeius.
derivation: Jason (Aesonides) asks Aeetes who a particular warrior is; Aeetes answers, with speech tag 'ait' dropped after 'Carmeius.' The reply 'quem rogitas, Carmeius' is the speaker's own contiguous words naming the man; cut before the following elaboration 'mos comminus arma semper habere viro...'.

question: Quis precor hic toto iamdudum fervere campo quem tueor quemque ipsa vides? nam te quoque tali attonitam virtute reor.
answer: Ipsum Aesoniden cernis, soror, aequore tanto debita cognati repetit qui vellera Phrixi nec nunc laude prior generis nec sanguine quisquam.
derivation: Medea (disguised Juno frames her: 'tunc his germanam adgreditur ceu nescia dictis:' dropped as narration) asks who the raging warrior is - a genuine interrogative (quis). Juno's reply frame 'contra aspera Iuno reddit... ait' is dropped as a speech tag; kept the contiguous answering span 'ipsum ... Aesoniden cernis, soror ... sanguine quisquam.' which directly identifies the man (Aesonides/Jason seeking Phrixus's fleece). Cut at the first full stop after 'quisquam'; what follows ('aspicis ut Minyas inter...') turns to a fresh rhetorical question and elaboration, so it is excluded. First word capitalized; no Latin altered, reordered, or invented.

question: Quis fragor hic? quaenam tantae, dic, virgo, ruinae?
answer: Hunc tibi postremum nostri parat ira parentis.
derivation: Jason (Aesonides), hearing the dragon stirred up, asks Medea a genuine interrogative (quis/quaenam, with imperative dic). Dropped the speech tag 'exclamat stricto Aesonides stans frigidus ense' and the answer's tag 'illa tacet retinens tandemque ait angue represso'. Answer cut to its first sentence ending at the full stop after 'parentis'; what follows ('heu miser, heu tantis iterum mihi care periclis...') is lament/elaboration, not the answer. The reply directly identifies the disturbance ('hunc... postremum') as the last monster her father's wrath has prepared. No editorial brackets or inline verse numbers fell inside either span.

question: Quis rubor iste poli? quod tam lugubre refulsit sidus?
answer: Ipsius en oculos et lumina torva draconis aspicis.
derivation: Jason, seeing the sudden flame and gleaming darkness, asks 'quis rubor iste poli? quod tam lugubre refulsit sidus?' (lines 58-60). The intervening speech tag 'ait, reddit trepido cui talia virgo:' is framing/narration and is dropped. Medea answers directly: the answer window ends at the first full stop ('aspicis.'); what follows ('ille suis haec vibrat fulgura cristis...') elaborates on the dragon and is cut. The dangling every-5-lines verse number 60 was stripped.

question: Mulier, filius tuus adversus te rogat; quid dicis? Est filius tuus an non?
answer: Non est meus filius sed peregrinum eum suscepi.
derivation: King's direct question to the mother in court, answered directly by her. Frame 'Cui et dixit:' and 'Quae dixit:' dropped. Kept the king's full utterance contiguous (including 'Mulier, filius tuus adversus te rogat; quid dicis?') so the interrogative 'Est filius tuus an non?' has its setting and referent.

question: Est filius tuus an non?
answer: Non est filius meus.
derivation: King's second direct question (after the son's full account) and the mother's direct answer. Frames 'dicit mulieri denuo:' and 'Quae dixit:' dropped.

question: Et quae est facultas tua, mulier?
answer: Usque ad mille solidos.
derivation: King's direct question about her means, answered directly. Frames 'Dicit ei rex:' and 'Quae respondit:' dropped.

question: Quis ergo huic consuetudini, qua nunc Graecis actionibus aures curiae exurdantur, ianuam patefecit?
answer: Ut opinor, Molo rhetor, qui studia M. Ciceronis acuit.
derivation: Author poses and answers his own question. Question is the verbatim interrogative sentence; first word capitalized. Answer cut at the full direct response 'Molo rhetor, qui studia M. Ciceronis acuit'; the following ':' introduces elaboration ('eum namque ante omnes... auditum constat') which is justification, not the direct answer, so it is excluded. 'ut opinor' is the author's hedged assertion, part of the answer, kept.

question: Quid ergo restituta continentia, quid repetita industria profecit?
answer: Crebras scilicet uictorias et multa tropaea peperit ex eo hoste, cuius tergum sub ambitioso imperatore Romano militi uidere non contigerat.
derivation: Author asks what restored discipline achieved and answers himself. Question is the verbatim interrogative sentence. Answer is the single sentence that follows, ending at the first full stop; it directly names the result (frequent victories and many trophies). First words capitalized; no interior content omitted.

question: Si dimicandum necne esset contrariis inter uos sententiis dissedissetis, utrum quod consul an quod praetor imperasset maius habiturum fuerit momentum?
answer: Non facere se controuersiam quin priores partes consulis essent futurae.
derivation: Calatinus questions Valerius. Dropped the asking-frame "'quaero' inquit, 'Valeri, a te," (narration of the act of asking) and kept the operative interrogative (si-protasis plus utrum...an interrogative). Answer dropped the speech tag 'respondit Valerius'; the indirect-discourse reply directly concedes the consul's role was the greater. First words capitalized.

question: Si diuersa auspicia accepissetis, cuius magis auspicio staretur?
answer: Item consulis.
derivation: Calatinus' second question to Valerius. Dropped the frame "'age deinde' inquit Calatinus,". Question kept verbatim. Answer: the interposed speech tag 'respondit Valerius' was removed, leaving Valerius' own contiguous words 'item' and 'consulis' in source order, directly answering 'by whose auspices': the consul's. First word capitalized.

question: Age, si uentum fuerit?
answer: Non renuntiabo.
derivation: Direct exchange in the Piso narrative: the crowd, pressing him whether he would declare Palicanus elected consul, asks the quoted interrogative 'age, si uentum fuerit?' and Piso answers with the quoted refusal 'non renuntiabo'. Speech frames dropped: the preceding 'deinde, cum perseueranter instarent ac dicerent' before the question, and the trailing 'inquit' after the answer. First word capitalized and terminal punctuation normalized (? on the question, full stop on the answer). The indirect-discourse setup ('Palicanum num... renuntiaturus esset interrogaretur') is narration, not quoted utterance, so it is not stitched in.

question: Quid? si te Gracchus templo Iouis optimi maximi faces subdere iussisset, obsecuturusne illius uoluntati propter istam, quam iactas, familiaritatem fuisti?
answer: Numquam istud Gracchus imperasset.
derivation: Laelius questions Blossius about his loyalty to Gracchus. Dropped the speech-tag framing 'atque is dixisset:' before the question and the interleaved 'inquit' in the answer; normalized initial capitalization ('quid'->'Quid', 'numquam'->'Numquam'). Question is a verbatim direct interrogative (note 'quid?' and the -ne in 'obsecuturusne'); answer is Blossius's verbatim direct reply, ending at the first full stop, after which narration resumes ('satis, immo etiam nimium...').

question: Quantas tandem tibi Athenae per te libertatem consecutae gratias debebunt?
answer: Di faciant ut quantas ipse illis debeo uidear retulisse.
derivation: Thrasybulus, freeing Athens from the Thirty Tyrants, is asked by one of his confederates how great a debt of gratitude the city will owe him. Dropped the speech-tag framing 'et quidam e consciis dixisset' (the angle brackets on '<e>' stripped, word kept) before the question, and 'respondit' before the answer. The question is a genuine direct interrogative ('Quantas... gratias debebunt?'); the answer is the full operative reply sentence (ends at the first full stop, after 'retulisse'); nothing follows within the utterance. Capitalized first words and normalized terminal punctuation.

question: Cur solus linguam suam cohiberet?
answer: Quia dixisse me aliquando paenituit, tacuisse numquam.
derivation: Xenocrates is asked why he alone kept silent. Dropped the asking-frame 'uno ex his quaerente' and the interior speech tag 'inquit'. Question is the author's indirect interrogative 'cur solus linguam suam cohiberet' (verbatim, capitalized, '?' added). Answer is his quoted reply; it ends the sentence, nothing trimmed.

question: An facta hominum deos fallerent?
answer: Ne cogitata quidem.
derivation: Thales is asked whether men's deeds escape the gods. Dropped the asking-frame 'interrogatus' and trailing tag 'inquit'. Stripped the editorial brackets in 'ne cogitata <quidem>' keeping 'quidem'. Cut the authorial gloss that follows ('ut non solum manus...') since it is Valerius's elaboration, not the reply.

question: Quisnam esset beatus?
answer: Nemo ex his, quos tu felices existimas, sed eum in illo numero reperies, qui a te ex miseris constare creditur.
derivation: Anaxagoras is asked who is happy. Dropped the asking-frame 'interroganti cuidam' and the interior tag 'inquit'. Answer is his full quoted reply through the first full stop; cut the authorial elaboration that follows ('non erit ille diuitiis et honoribus abundans...').

question: Cum dux Romanorum magnas secum maritimas trahens copias aduenerit, an cum eo confligere debeat?
answer: Non esse dubium quin oporteret.
derivation: Hannibal's agent asks the Carthaginian senate whether they should fight. Dropped the asking-frame 'consulit uos inquit Hannibal'; kept the contiguous interrogative the agent poses. Answer is the senate's verbatim reply with its narrating frame 'adclamauit uniuersus senatus' dropped; it answers the question ('no doubt they ought to').

question: Quanto ergo eam minoris fore existimas, si decem arbusculas inde succidero?
answer: Ipso tricies sestertio.
derivation: Crassus puts a genuine direct interrogative to Domitius (quanto... minoris fore existimas, si... succidero?), and Domitius answers with a price. Dropped the framing 'inquit' inside the question and the narrative speaker-attribution 'Domitius' that follows the answer. Stripped editorial brackets in 'qu<ant>o' -> 'Quanto' (capitalized as first word). Normalized terminal punctuation: kept the question mark on the question and put a full stop on the answer. The preceding indirect question (quanti... aestimaret interrogauit) and its reply 'sexagies sestertio' are narrated indirect discourse, not a verbatim interrogative utterance, so excluded; the chosen pair is the fully direct-speech exchange.

locus: Varro De Lingua Latina fragment 6 (Liber IX)
question: Et ubi auctoritas maiorum genus tibi non demonstraverit, quid ibi faciendum est?
answer: Potestatis nostrae est illis rebus dare genera, quae ex natura genus non habent.
derivation: The text poses a real interrogative (quid ibi faciendum est?) about what to do when the authority of the ancients does not show the gender, and answers it with Varro's reply. Dropped the framing tag 'Scripsit Varro ad Ciceronem:' that narrates the answering; kept the question's setup ('Et ubi auctoritas maiorum genus tibi non demonstraverit') so 'ibi' has its referent. Answer ends at the full stop; nothing was trimmed from it (the section opens the next paragraph, fragment 7 A).

question: Quid enim similius potest videri indiligenti quam duo verba haec suis et suis?
answer: Quae non sunt, quod alterum significat suere, alterum suem.
derivation: Authorial rhetorical question asking what could seem more alike than 'suis' and 'suis', immediately resolved by the author himself: they are not alike, because one means 'suere' and the other 'suem'. Question taken verbatim; answer is the single following sentence (to the full stop) that directly resolves the question; the next sentence ('Itaque similia vocibus...') turns to a new generalization and is excluded.

question: Io bucco! Quis me iubilat?
answer: Vicinus tuus antiquus.
derivation: Quoted verse of Aprissius, introduced by the dropped framing tag 'Aprissius ait'. One party hails ('Io bucco!'), the other asks the genuine interrogative 'Quis me iubilat?' ('Who hails me?'), and the first answers 'Vicinus tuus antiquus.' ('Your old neighbor.'). The hail 'Io bucco!' is kept as verbatim setup so 'me iubilat' has a referent. The answer is the complete contiguous reply (one sentence); nothing cut after it. All other interrogatives in this book (e.g. 'Quis is est qui meum nomen nuncupat?', 'Quis tu es, mulier...', 'Sponden tuam gnatam...', 'Meministin te spondere...', 'Lumen iubarne... cerno') are isolated illustrative quotations with no answering line and were dropped.

locus: Plautus, Curculio (quoted at Varro, De Lingua Latina 7.2)
question: Sed quid tibi est?
answer: Lien enecat, renes dolent, pulmones distrahuntur.
derivation: A two-speaker exchange from Curculio quoted by Varro to illustrate dividia/distrahuntur. The editorial speaker-change dash (—) was stripped as a drama marker. Question kept as the first speaker's full contiguous utterance (interrogative quid tibi est?). Answer is the second speaker's reply, which genuinely answers by listing the ailments; no preamble to skip and nothing follows the reply in the quoted fragment.

question: Quid noctis videtur?
answer: In altisono caeli clipeo temo superat stellas sublimen agens etiam atque etiam noctis iter.
derivation: Interrogative quid noctis videtur? ('what time of night is it?') answered by a description of the temo (Wain) overtopping the stars, which Varro glosses as indicating deep night (Hic multam noctem ostendere volt a temonis motu). The editorial speaker-change dash was stripped; verse line-initial capitals (In, Caeli, Stellas, Atque) were lowercased as presentation normalization. Answer is the full contiguous reply through the verse fragment; nothing of the utterance was ellipted.

question: Ex qua parte oporteat simile esse verbum, a voce an a significatione?
answer: A voce.
derivation: Authorial objection-and-reply. Dropped the asking-frame 'Quod rogant' at the start and the answer-tag 'respondemus' (narration of asking/answering). The interrogative is the alternative question 'a voce an a significatione'; punctuation normalized to '?'. The answer is the direct operative response 'a voce' (capitalized, terminal punctuation added). Cut everything after the semicolon ('sed tamen nonnunquam quaerimus genere similiane sint...'), which is a qualifying digression, not the answer to the posed question.

question: Cur non dicamus mane manius manissime?
answer: In tempore vere magis et minus esse non potest, ante et post potest.
derivation: Authorial objection-and-reply. Dropped the asking-frame 'Quod rogant,' at the start; kept the 'cur' interrogative core and omitted the trailing 'item de vesperi' so the utterance stays a clean single contiguous question (normalized capitalization and terminal '?'). The answer is the operative explanation ending at the first full stop; cut the following 'Itaque prius est hora prima quam secunda...' onward, which elaborates with examples rather than directly answering.

question: Quid vos hic? num feriae sementivae otiosos huc adduxerunt, ut patres et avos solebant nostros?
answer: Nos vero, ut arbitror, eadem causa quae te, rogatio aeditumi.
derivation: Varro asks (speech tag 'inquam' dropped from inside the question). Agrius answers, with the speech tag 'inquit Agrius' dropped. Question span is the two interrogative sentences of Varro's utterance; answer is Agrius's full reply sentence. Following the answer Agrius continues 'Itaque si ita est...' which moves to new business, so the window stops at the first full stop.

question: Vos, qui multas perambulastis terras, ecquam cultiorem Italia vidistis?
answer: Ego vero nullam arbitror esse quae tam tota sit culta.
derivation: Agrasius asks; the trailing speech tag 'inquit' is dropped. Answer is Agrius's reply (narrative tag 'Agrius' dropped); cut at the first full stop, after which 'Primum cum orbis terrae divisus sit...' begins a long digression elaborating why, which is not part of the direct answer.

question: Quid potero facere, si istius modi mi fundus hereditati obvenerit, quo minus pestilentia noceat?
answer: Istuc vel ego possum respondere; vendas, quot assibus possis, aut si nequeas, relinquas.
derivation: Fundanius asks (speech tag 'inquit' dropped). Agrius answers, explicitly marked 'inquit Agrius' (dropped); his reply is the full sentence. After this Scrofa ('At Scrofa, Vitandum, inquit...') resumes the treatise, so the answer window ends at Agrius's full stop.

question: Quae tria? an ea quae mihi here dixisti de pastoricia re?
answer: Ista quae coeperat hic disserere, quae esset origo, quae dignitas, quae ars.
derivation: Murrius asks which three topics were meant; 'ille' (Cossinius) answers by enumerating them (origo, dignitas, ars). Dropped the speech tags 'inquit Murrius' and 'inquit ille' as framing/narration. The answer ends at the enumeration; immediately after 'ars' the text has a lacuna marker (***) then a new speaker ('Ego vero, inquam, dicam...'), which is excluded; trailing '***' stripped and a terminal stop normalized in place of the comma.

question: Dum diribentur suffragia, vis potius villae publicae utamur umbra, quam privati candidati tabella dimidiata aedificemus nobis?
answer: Opinor non solum, quod dicitur, "malum consilium consultori est pessimum", sed etiam bonum consilium, qui consulit et qui consulitur, bonum habendum.
derivation: Axius proposes (genuine yes/no interrogative 'vis...?') waiting in the shade of the villa publica; Varro answers affirmatively that good counsel benefits both parties (followed in the text by 'Itaque imus, venimus in villam'). Dropped framing tags 'Axius mihi,' / 'inquit,' from the question and 'inquam,' from the answer; normalized initial capital and terminal '?'. Answer ends at first full stop, before 'Itaque imus...'.

question: Recipis nos in tuum ornithona, ubi sedes inter aves?
answer: Ego vero te praesertim, quoius aues hospitales etiam nunc ructor, quas mihi apposuisti paucis ante diebus in Villa Reatina ad lacum Velini eunti de controversiis Interamnatium et Reatinorum.
derivation: Axius asks Appius a genuine yes/no question (Recipis nos...?); Appius answers affirmatively ('Ego vero te praesertim' = yes, you especially). Dropped framing 'inquit,' from the question and 'Ille,' / 'inquit,' from the answer; normalized capitalization. Answer cut at first full stop ('...Reatinorum.'), before Appius turns to a fresh question 'Sed non haec... villa...?'.

question: Omnipotens genitor, qui solus ab aethere summo Cuncta moues, qui res hominum, curasque recenses; Dum Teucros traheret fortuna inimica, recordor, Spondebas finem aerumnis, rebusque salutem. Nec tua te promissa, pater, sententia fallit; Namque omnes gaudere sacra tres pace per annos Uiderunt Italae nullo discrimine partes; Uerum ad siderei missurum culmina caeli Pollicitus magnum Aenean, meritumque ferebas Illaturum astris: quid nunc sub pectore uersas? Iamque optat matura polos Aeneia uirtus?
answer: Tandemque malis, Iunone secunda, Imposui finem: nunc stat sententia menti, Qua ductorem alto Phrygium succedere caelo Institui, et firma est.
derivation: Venus's entire speech to Jupiter, quoted verbatim and contiguous as the question (whole-speech-as-question), recalling his promise to raise Aeneas to the stars and ending in the genuine interrogative 'quid nunc sub pectore uersas?'. Stripped: framing tag 'sic ore locuta est:' before it, the opening quote mark, and the dangling inline verse number '600'; terminal punctuation normalized to '?'. Jupiter's reply opens with a non-answering preamble recalling his love for Aeneas ('Quantum, Cytherea... Nosti: et saepe equidem indolui commotus amore, Nata, tuo:'), so the answer-start is advanced to the operative answering sentence 'tandemque malis... Institui, et firma est' (Jupiter confirms he has decided to let Aeneas ascend to heaven); cut at the first full stop, before 'numeroque inferre deorum Constat...'. Stripped the framing 'Olli... uerba ferens:', the opening quote mark, and the inline verse number '610'; capitalized 'Tandemque' as first word.

question: Si quid huic acciderit, quem in eius locum substituetis?
answer: Te, Q. Catule.
derivation: Catulus, dissuading the lex granting Pompey the pirate command, asks the contio whom they would substitute if anything happened to Pompey; the whole assembly shouts back the answer. Dropped the speech-framing narration before the question (the indirect-speech setup ending '...neque omnia in uno reponenda adiecissetque:') and the framing 'subclamavit universa contio:' before the answer, plus the trailing narration 'Tum ille victus consensu omnium...'. Question normalized to initial capital and '?'; answer normalized to initial capital and terminal '.'. Both utterances are verbatim and contiguous.

question: O qui res hominumque deumque aeternis regis imperiis, et fulmine terres, quid meus Aeneas in te committere tantum, quid Troes potuere, quibus, tot funera passis, cunctus ob Italiam terrarum clauditur orbis? Certe hinc Romanos olim, volventibus annis, hinc fore ductores, revocato a sanguine Teucri, qui mare, qui terras omni dicione tenerent, pollicitus, quae te, genitor, sententia vertit? Hoc equidem occasum Troiae tristisque ruinas solabar, fatis contraria fata rependens; nunc eadem fortuna viros tot casibus actos insequitur. Quem das finem, rex magne, laborum? Antenor potuit, mediis elapsus Achivis, Illyricos penetrare sinus, atque intima tutus regna Liburnorum, et fontem superare Timavi, unde per ora novem vasto cum murmure montis it mare proruptum et pelago premit arva sonanti. Hic tamen ille urbem Patavi sedesque locavit Teucrorum, et genti nomen dedit, armaque fixit Troia; nunc placida compostus pace quiescit: nos, tua progenies, caeli quibus adnuis arcem, navibus amissis, unius ob iram prodimur atque Italis longe disiungimur oris. Hic pietatis honos? Sic nos in sceptra reponis?
answer: Parce metu, Cytherea: manent immota tuorum fata tibi; cernes urbem et promissa Lavini moenia, sublimemque feres ad sidera caeli magnanimum Aenean; neque me sententia vertit.
derivation: Venus's entire speech (whole-speech-as-question) kept verbatim and contiguous; dropped framing 'adloquitur Venus:' before it. The pleading parenthetical '(infandum!)' is editorial-aside punctuation; only the words 'navibus amissis' retained in source order. Jupiter's reply: dropped framing 'dehinc talia fatur:'; answer ends at the first full stop after 'neque me sententia vertit' (which directly answers Venus's 'quae te sententia vertit?'); what follows ('Hic tibi... fabor enim...') is the long prophecy digression, cut.

question: Heus iuvenes, monstrate mearum vidistis si quam hic errantem forte sororum, succinctam pharetra et maculosae tegmine lyncis, aut spumantis apri cursum clamore prementem.
answer: Nulla tuarum audita mihi neque visa sororum.
derivation: Venus (disguised) asks whether the youths have seen one of her sisters; dropped framing 'inquit'. Aeneas's reply opens by directly answering 'Nulla tuarum audita mihi neque visa sororum' (cut at the first sentence break/dash); what follows ('O quam te memorem, virgo?...') turns to addressing her divinity and a separate plea, so it is omitted. Dropped framing 'Veneris contra sic filius orsus:'.

question: Sed vos qui tandem, quibus aut venistis ab oris, quove tenetis iter?
answer: Sum pius Aeneas, raptos qui ex hoste Penates classe veho mecum, fama super aethera notus. Italiam quaero patriam et genus ab Iove summo.
derivation: Venus asks Aeneas his identity and origin; the interrogative span is quoted verbatim. Aeneas's reply opens with a non-answering preamble ('O dea, si prima repetens... ante diem clauso componat Vesper Olympo' = the tale is too long to tell, plus the 'Nos Troia antiqua... adpulit oris' setup), so the answer start is advanced to the operative answering sentences 'Sum pius Aeneas... Italiam quaero patriam et genus ab Iove summo'; cut before 'Bis denis Phrygium...' which elaborates the voyage. Dropped framing 'Quaerenti talibus ille suspirans...'.

question: Quid, o pulcherrime coniunx, sollicitas aegram et tua tristia dicta timentem? si mihi, quae quondam fuerat quamque esse decebat, uis in amore foret, non hoc mihi namque negares, omnipotens, quin et pugnae subducere Turnum et Dauno possem incolumem seruare parenti. nunc pereat Teucrisque pio det sanguine poenas. ille tamen nostra deducit origine nomen Pilumnusque illi quartus pater, et tua larga saepe manu multisque onerauit limina donis.
answer: Si mora praesentis leti tempusque caduco oratur iuueni meque hoc ita ponere sentis, tolle fuga Turnum atque instantibus eripe fatis: hactenus indulsisse uacat.
derivation: Juno's entire reply-plea to Jupiter, quoted contiguously and verbatim; only the speech tag 'cui Iuno summissa:' was dropped and the first word capitalized. Her speech is an extended plea to spare Turnus (the opening 'quid... sollicitas?' is reproachful; the operative request is 'subducere Turnum... seruare parenti' followed by entreaty on Turnus's behalf). Jupiter answers it: I cut the tag 'cui rex aetherii breuiter sic fatur Olympi:' and ended the answer at the first full stop after 'uacat', which is the genuine grant of a delay ('tolle fuga Turnum atque instantibus eripe fatis: hactenus indulsisse uacat'). What follows the cut ('sin altior istis sub precibus uenia ulla latet... spes pascis inanis') is the refusal of anything more than the delay, an elaboration/limitation, so it is excluded from the answer window. The terminal punctuation of the question was normalized to a question mark.

question: Quae iam finis erit, coniunx? quid denique restat? indigetem Aenean scis ipsa et scire fateris deberi caelo fatisque ad sidera tolli. quid struis? aut qua spe gelidis in nubibus haeres? mortalin decuit uiolari uulnere diuum? aut ensem (quid enim sine te Iuturna ualeret?) ereptum reddi Turno et uim crescere uictis? desine iam tandem precibusque inflectere nostris, ne te tantus edit tacitam dolor et mihi curae saepe tuo dulci tristes ex ore recursent. uentum ad supremum est. terris agitare uel undis Troianos potuisti, infandum accendere bellum, deformare domum et luctu miscere hymenaeos: ulterius temptare ueto.
answer: Et nunc cedo equidem pugnasque exosa relinquo.
derivation: Whole-speech-as-question: Jupiter's entire speech to Juno, quoted verbatim and contiguous. Stripped framing narration before ('Iunonem interea rex omnipotentis Olympi / adloquitur fulua pugnas de nube tuentem:') and after ('sic Iuppiter orsus;'). Speech contains genuine interrogatives (quae iam finis erit, quid struis, qua spe haeres) and the operative demand 'desine iam tandem... ulterius temptare ueto'. For the answer, Juno's reply opens with a non-answering self-justifying preamble ('ista quidem quia nota mihi tua... inuita reliqui', then her account of advising Iuturna and her oath by the Styx); per the skip-non-answering-preamble guidance the answer's start is advanced to the operative sentence in which she actually yields. The answer ends at the first full stop; what follows ('illud te, nulla fati quod lege tenetur, pro Latio obtestor...') turns from yielding to making her own request about names and is not part of the answer. Editorial-bracket items elsewhere in the speech (e.g. '(fateor)', '(esto)') fall outside both spans.

question: quisquis es, amissos hinc iam obliuiscere Graios (noster eris) mihique haec edissere uera roganti: quo molem hanc immanis equi statuere? quis auctor? quidue petunt? quae religio? aut quae machina belli?
answer: hanc pro Palladio moniti, pro numine laeso effigiem statuere, nefas quae triste piaret.
derivation: Priam (named in narration 'fatur Priamus', dropped) asks Sinon why the horse was built and what they seek. Sinon's reply opens with a long non-answering preamble: an oath ('uos, aeterni ignes... testor numen') and a digression about his right to break Greek faith and about Palladium-theft and Calchas, none of which answers 'why did they build this image'. Advanced the answer start past all of that to the operative answering sentence at 2.183-184, which directly answers 'quo... statuere? quidue petunt?'. Stopped at the first full stop after 'piaret'; what follows ('hanc tamen immensam Calchas attollere molem...') explains its size, a further elaboration. Speech tag 'dixerat. ille... ait' omitted from the question; 'roganti' kept as it is part of Priam's framed utterance setup giving 'haec' a referent.

question: quo res summa loco, Panthu? quam prendimus arcem?
answer: uenit summa dies et ineluctabile tempus Dardaniae.
derivation: Aeneas asks Panthus where the main fight stands and which citadel they can hold. Narration 'uix ea fatus eram gemitu cum talia reddit:' dropped as a speech tag. Answer is the reply's first sentence (to the first full stop after 'Dardaniae'); what follows ('fuimus Troes, fuit Ilium...') elaborates on the fall of the city rather than answering the locational question.

question: Da propriam, Thymbraee, domum; da moenia fessis et genus et mansuram urbem; serua altera Troiae Pergama, reliquias Danaum atque immitis Achilli. quem sequimur? quoue ire iubes? ubi ponere sedes? da, pater, augurium atque animis inlabere nostris?
answer: Dardanidae duri, quae uos a stirpe parentum prima tulit tellus, eadem uos ubere laeto accipiet reduces. antiquam exquirite matrem.
derivation: Aeneas's whole prayer-plea to Apollo at Delos is the question, quoted entire and contiguous (da propriam... inlabere nostris), containing the explicit interrogatives quem sequimur? quoue ire iubes? ubi ponere sedes? Narration frame stripped: opening 'Templa dei saxo uenerabar structa uetusto:' before the speech, and 'uix ea fatus eram... uox fertur ad auris:' between speeches. The answer is Apollo's oracular reply; window cut at the first full stop after the operative directive 'antiquam exquirite matrem.' which answers ubi ponere sedes; what follows ('hic domus Aeneae cunctis dominabitur oris...') elaborates the prophecy and is omitted. Inline verse numbers (85, 90, 95) stripped.

question: Uerane te facies, uerus mihi nuntius adfers, nate dea? uiuisne? aut, si lux alma recessit, Hector ubi est?
answer: Uiuo equidem uitamque extrema per omnia duco; ne dubita, nam uera uides.
derivation: Andromache asks the newly-arrived Aeneas whether he is truly alive (interrogatives uiuisne? Hector ubi est?). Her speech quoted contiguous; the narrative tail 'dixit, lacrimasque effudit... clamore locum' is dropped as framing. Aeneas's reply answers directly; window taken as the operative answering sentences 'uiuo equidem... nam uera uides' (his own framing 'uix pauca furenti subicio et raris turbatus uocibus hisco:' stripped before). The reply continues with a counter-question 'heu! quis te casus deiectam coniuge tanto excipit...' which is omitted. Inline verse numbers (310, 315) stripped.

question: Troiugena, interpres diuum, qui numina Phoebi, qui tripodas Clarii et laurus, qui sidera sentis et uolucrum linguas et praepetis omina pennae, fare age (namque omnis cursum mihi prospera dixit religio, et cuncti suaserunt numine diui Italiam petere et terras temptare repostas; sola nouum dictuque nefas Harpyia Celaeno prodigium canit et tristis denuntiat iras obscenamque famem), quae prima pericula uito? quidue sequens tantos possim superare labores?
answer: Principio Italiam, quam tu iam rere propinquam uicinosque, ignare, paras inuadere portus, longa procul longis uia diuidit inuia terris.
derivation: Aeneas's whole address to the seer Helenus is the question, quoted entire and contiguous including its parenthetical (namque... famem) which is part of the utterance, ending in the explicit interrogatives quae prima pericula uito? quidue... superare labores? Frame stripped: 'his uatem adgredior dictis ac talia quaeso:' before, and the narration of Helenus sacrificing/leading (hic Helenus caesis... canit diuino ex ore sacerdos:) between speeches. Helenus's reply opens with a non-answering preamble ('Nate dea... expediam dictis; prohibent nam cetera Parcae scire Helenum farique uetat Saturnia Iuno.') framing what he will reveal; the answer's start is advanced past it to the operative 'principio Italiam... inuia terris.' answering quae prima pericula (the first peril: Italy is far, not near). Cut at that full stop; the subsequent dangers (ante et Trinacria lentandus remus...) are omitted. Inline verse numbers (360-380) stripped.

question: Dissimulare etiam sperasti, perfide, tantum posse nefas tacitusque mea decedere terra? nec te noster amor nec te data dextera quondam nec moritura tenet crudeli funere Dido? quin etiam hiberno moliri sidere classem et mediis properas Aquilonibus ire per altum, crudelis? quid, si non arua aliena domosque ignotas peteres, et Troia antiqua maneret, Troia per undosum peteretur classibus aequor? mene fugis? per ego has lacrimas dextramque tuam te (quando aliud mihi iam miserae nihil ipsa reliqui), per conubia nostra, per inceptos hymenaeos, si bene quid de te merui, fuit aut tibi quicquam dulce meum, miserere domus labentis et istam, oro, si quis adhuc precibus locus, exue mentem. te propter Libycae gentes Nomadumque tyranni odere, infensi Tyrii; te propter eundem exstinctus pudor et, qua sola sidera adibam, fama prior. cui me moribundam deseris hospes (hoc solum nomen quoniam de coniuge restat)? quid moror? an mea Pygmalion dum moenia frater destruat aut captam ducat Gaetulus Iarbas? saltem si qua mihi de te suscepta fuisset ante fugam suboles, si quis mihi paruulus aula luderet Aeneas, qui te tamen ore referret, non equidem omnino capta ac deserta uiderer.
answer: Sed nunc Italiam magnam Gryneus Apollo, Italiam Lyciae iussere capessere sortes; hic amor, haec patria est.
derivation: Dido genuinely asks (mene fugis? cui me moribundam deseris hospes? etc.), so this qualifies as a whole-speech-as-question. The question is her entire speech verbatim and contiguous, framing stripped: the leading speech tag 'tandem his Aenean compellat uocibus ultro:' is dropped, and the closing 'Dixerat.' (4.331, which begins Aeneas's narration) is not part of her utterance. Aeneas's reply opens with a non-answering preamble that praises her and refuses to forget her ('ego te... numquam, regina, negabo promeritam... et recidiua manu posuissem Pergama uictis', 4.333-344), which does not answer why he flees; so the answer's start advances to the operative answering sentence 'sed nunc Italiam... hic amor, haec patria est.' (4.345-347), ending at the first full stop after 'est'. What follows the cut is 'si te Karthaginis arces Phoenissam...' continuing his justification.

question: Entelle, heroum quondam fortissime frustra, tantane tam patiens nullo certamine tolli dona sines? ubi nunc nobis deus ille, magister nequiquam memoratus, Eryx? ubi fama per omnem Trinacriam et spolia illa tuis pendentia tectis?
answer: Non laudis amor nec gloria cessit pulsa metu; sed enim gelidus tardante senecta sanguis hebet, frigentque effetae in corpore uires.
derivation: Acestes rebukes Entellus with a speech of genuine interrogatives (tantane... sines? ubi... Eryx? ubi fama...?); quoted whole and contiguous as the question. Reply is introduced by the framing tag 'ille sub haec:' (dropped). Answer starts at Entellus's operative answering words 'Non laudis amor...' and stops at the first full stop after 'in corpore uires.' What follows ('si mihi quae quondam fuerat...') turns to a conditional wish about lost youth, elaboration rather than direct answer, so it is cut.

question: Dic, o uirgo, quid uult concursus ad amnem? quidue petunt animae? uel quo discrimine ripas hae linquunt, illae remis uada liuida uerrunt?
answer: Anchisa generate, deum certissima proles, Cocyti stagna alta uides Stygiamque paludem, di cuius iurare timent et fallere numen. haec omnis, quam cernis, inops inhumataque turba est; portitor ille Charon; hi, quos uehit unda, sepulti.
derivation: Aeneas asks the Sibyl about the crowd at the river. Dropped the speech tag 'ait' embedded in the question line. Answer begins at the Sibyl's reply 'Anchisa generate...'; cut after 'hi, quos uehit unda, sepulti.' (first full explanation of the crowd), before she goes on to 'nec ripas datur...' about the hundred years' wait.

question: Quis te, Palinure, deorum eripuit nobis medioque sub aequore mersit? dic age. namque mihi, fallax haud ante repertus, hoc uno responso animum delusit Apollo, qui fore te ponto incolumem finisque canebat uenturum Ausonios. en haec promissa fides est?
answer: Neque te Phoebi cortina fefellit, dux Anchisiade, nec me deus aequore mersit. namque gubernaclum multa ui forte reuulsum, cui datus haerebam custos cursusque regebam, praecipitans traxi mecum.
derivation: Aeneas asks Palinurus which god drowned him. Dropped narration framing ('sic prior adloquitur'). Answer begins at Palinurus's reply (dropping the tag 'ille autem'): he answers no god drowned him, the torn-off tiller dragged him down. Cut after 'praecipitans traxi mecum.' (first full sentence), before he digresses to the storm and his plea for burial.

question: Deiphobe armipotens, genus alto a sanguine Teucri, quis tam crudelis optauit sumere poenas? cui tantum de te licuit?
answer: Sed me fata mea et scelus exitiale Lacaenae his mersere malis; illa haec monimenta reliquit.
derivation: Aeneas asks the mutilated Deiphobus who inflicted such cruelty. Took only the interrogative opening of his address (dropping the following narrative 'mihi fama suprema nocte tulit...'). Skipped Deiphobus's non-answering preamble 'nihil o tibi, amice, relictum; omnia Deiphobo soluisti et funeris umbris.'; the operative answer names the culprit (the Spartan woman, Helen). Cut after 'illa haec monimenta reliquit.', before 'namque ut supremam falsa inter gaudia noctem egerimus...' (the long narrative of the fall of Troy).

question: Quae scelerum facies? O uirgo, effare; quibusue urgentur poenis? quis tantus plangor ad auras?
answer: Cnosius haec Rhadamanthus habet durissima regna castigatque auditque dolos subigitque fateri quae quis apud superos furto laetatus inani distulit in seram commissa piacula mortem.
derivation: Aeneas asks the Sibyl what crimes and punishments produce the cries from Tartarus. Skipped the Sibyl's preamble ('dux inclute Teucrum, nulli fas casto sceleratum insistere limen; sed me cum lucis Hecate praefecit Auernis, ipsa deum poenas docuit...'), which states she may not enter but was taught, not what is punished. Answer begins at the operative description 'Cnosius haec Rhadamanthus...'; cut after the first full sentence ('...in seram commissa piacula mortem.'), before the catalogue continues with 'continuo sontis ultrix...'.

question: Dicite, felices animae tuque optime uates, quae regio Anchisen, quis habet locus? illius ergo uenimus et magnos Erebi tranauimus amnis.
answer: Nulli certa domus; lucis habitamus opacis, riparumque toros et prata recentia riuis incolimus. sed uos, si fert ita corde uoluntas, hoc superate iugum, et facili iam tramite sistam.
derivation: The Sibyl asks Musaeus and the blessed souls where Anchises dwells. Kept the verbatim setup 'illius ergo uenimus...' since it makes the question intelligible. Answer begins at Musaeus's reply (dropping the tag 'atque huic responsum paucis ita reddidit heros'): no fixed home, but cross this ridge and I will set you on an easy path. Whole reply is the answer; ends the speech at 'sistam.'

question: O pater, anne aliquas ad caelum hinc ire putandum est sublimis animas iterumque ad tarda reuerti corpora? quae lucis miseris tam dira cupido?
answer: Igneus est ollis uigor et caelestis origo seminibus, quantum non noxia corpora tardant terrenique hebetant artus moribundaque membra.
derivation: Aeneas asks Anchises why souls at Lethe should desire to return to bodies. Skipped Anchises's non-answering preamble 'dicam equidem nec te suspensum, nate, tenebo' (a promise to tell, not the answer) and the cosmological setup 'Principio caelum ac terras... mens agitat molem'. The operative answer to the desire for bodily life is the doctrine that a fiery vigor and heavenly origin animate the seeds, dulled by the body. Cut after 'moribundaque membra.', before 'hinc metuunt cupiuntque...' (elaboration of the consequences).

question: quid petitis? quae causa rates aut cuius egentis litus ad Ausonium tot per uada caerula uexit?
answer: diluuio ex illo tot uasta per aequora uecti dis sedem exiguam patriis litusque rogamus innocuum et cunctis undamque auramque patentem.
derivation: Latinus addresses the Trojan envoys and asks what they seek and what brought them. The question is the contiguous interrogative core of his speech (197-198); the preceding 'dicite, Dardanidae (neque enim nescimus...cursum)' framing/vocative and the following reassurances about Latinus's people and Dardanus's origins (199-211) are dropped, and the parenthetical is not stitched across. Ilioneus's reply (213-262) opens with a non-answering preamble denying they came by storm or error ('rex...nec fluctibus actos atra subegit hiems...nec sidus...fefellit') and recounting Aeneas and Troy's fall; the answer-window advances to the operative answering sentence (228-230), a single contiguous sentence stating their request, ending at the first full stop ('...patentem.'). What follows is 'non erimus regno indecores...' (assurances), which elaborates rather than answers.

question: Iuuenes, quae causa subegit ignotas temptare uias? quo tenditis? qui genus? unde domo? pacemne huc fertis an arma?
answer: Troiugenas ac tela uides inimica Latinis, quos illi bello profugos egere superbo. Euandrum petimus.
derivation: Pallas calls out from the mound and asks the arriving strangers who they are, where they are bound, their lineage, and whether they bring peace or war. Stripped framing 'et procul e tumulo:' before and the speech tag 'inquit' that interrupts mid-utterance after 'tenditis?'; the speaker's words are kept contiguous. Aeneas answers directly: they are Trojans whose weapons are hostile to the Latins, profugees, and they seek Euander. Stripped the narration 'tum pater Aeneas puppi sic fatur ab alta / paciferaeque manu ramum praetendit oliuae:' before the answer. Ended the answer at 'Euandrum petimus.' (first full stops giving the operative reply); the following 'ferte haec et dicite lectos Dardaniae uenisse duces socia arma rogantis' is an imperative request to relay a message, not part of answering the identity questions, so it is cut. Removed the dangling inline verse number 120.

question: Da, nate, petenti, quod tua cara parens domito te poscit Olympo. pinea silua mihi multos dilecta per annos, lucus in arce fuit summa, quo sacra ferebant, nigranti picea trabibusque obscurus acernis. has ego Dardanio iuueni, cum classis egeret, laeta dedi; nunc sollicitam timor anxius angit. solue metus atque hoc precibus sine posse parentem, ne cursu quassatae ullo neu turbine uenti uincantur: prosit nostris in montibus ortas.
answer: Immo, ubi defunctae finem portusque tenebunt Ausonios olim, quaecumque euaserit undis Dardaniumque ducem Laurentia uexerit arua, mortalem eripiam formam magnique iubebo aequoris esse deas, qualis Nereia Doto et Galatea secant spumantem pectore pontum.
derivation: Berecyntia's (Cybele's) whole plea to Jupiter is quoted verbatim and contiguous as the question, dropping the framing tag 'uocibus his adfata Iouem:'; verse numbers 85/90 stripped. Jupiter's reply ('filius huic contra, torquet qui sidera mundi:' framing dropped) opens with non-answering rhetorical deflection ('o genetrix, quo fata uocas? aut quid petis istis? mortaline manu factae immortale carinae fas habeant? certusque incerta pericula lustret Aeneas? cui tanta deo permissa potestas?'), so the answer start advances to the operative granting sentence beginning 'Immo,' which addresses her fear that the ships be destroyed by promising to transform them into sea-goddesses; window ends at the full stop after 'pontum.' (what follows is the narration 'dixerat idque ratum...'). Verse numbers 95/100 stripped.

question: Et quae tanta fuit Romam tibi causa videndi?
answer: Libertas, quae sera tamen respexit inertem, candidior postquam tondenti barba cadebat, respexit tamen et longo post tempore venit, postquam nos Amaryllis habet, Galatea reliquit.
derivation: Meliboeus asks a clean interrogative (quae ... causa) for Tityrus's reason for seeing Rome. Tityrus answers directly: Libertas (freedom). Verse numbers 30 and the speaker labels Meliboeus/Tityrus are stripped. Answer ends at the first full stop after reliquit; the following line (namque - fatebor enim - dum me Galatea tenebat...) begins elaboration on his prior servitude and is cut.

question: Quae nemora aut qui uos saltus habuere, puellae Naides, indigno cum Gallus amore peribat?
answer: Nam neque Parnasi uobis iuga, nam neque Pindi ulla moram fecere, neque Aonie Aganippe.
derivation: The poet asks the Naiads where they were while Gallus perished, and answers himself: it was not the ridges of Parnasus or Pindus or Aonian Aganippe that detained them. Inline verse number 10 (after 'peribat') and 5-line markers stripped. Answer ends at the full stop after 'Aganippe' (line 14).

question: Ecquis erit modus?
answer: Amor non talia curat, nec lacrimis crudelis Amor nec gramina riuis nec cytiso saturantur apes nec fronde capellae.
derivation: Pan asks whether there will be any limit, then answers within the same speech that Love does not care for such things. Speech tag 'inquit' dropped as framing. Answer runs to the full stop after 'capellae' (line 30); inline number 30 stripped.

question: Quid tum, si fuscus Amyntas?
answer: Et nigrae uiolae sunt et uaccinia nigra.
derivation: Gallus's parenthetical: 'what does it matter if Amyntas is swarthy?' answered immediately by 'violets too are dark and hyacinths are dark.' First word capitalization normalized on each field; answer ends at the parenthesis-closing full stop after 'nigra' (line 39).

question: Dic mihi, Damoeta, cuium pecus? An Meliboei?
answer: Non, verum Aegonos; nuper mihi tradidit Aegon.
derivation: Menalcas asks Damoetas whose the flock is (interrogative 'cuium pecus? An Meliboei?'); Damoetas answers directly that it is Aegon's. Speaker labels 'Menalcas'/'Damoetas' stripped. Answer is the full single-line reply; no preamble to skip. The remaining poem is an amoebean singing contest of capping statements, boasts, and unanswered riddles (e.g. the 'Dic quibus in terris' challenges at 104-107, which Palaemon declines to judge), so no further genuine Q&A pairs.

question: Saeuos Amor docuit natorum sanguine matrem commaculare manus; crudelis tu quoque, mater: crudelis mater magis, an puer improbus ille?
answer: Improbus ille puer; crudelis tu quoque, mater.
derivation: Disjunctive interrogative (crudelis mater magis, an puer improbus ille?) self-answered in the next line. Setup retained from the start of the sentence (Saeuos Amor docuit... commaculare manus; crudelis tu quoque, mater) so 'ille puer' (Amor/Cupid) and 'mater' (Medea) have referents and the comparison is intelligible. Answer is the full retort line; nothing cut from it. The verse-refrain lines (Incipe Maenalios...) flanking this stanza are stripped as scaffolding, as are the dangling inline line-numbers.

question: Scrobibus quae sint fastigia?
answer: ausim uel tenui uitem committere sulco; altior ac penitus terrae defigitur arbos, aesculus in primis, quae quantum uertice ad auras aetherias, tantum radice in Tartara tendit.
derivation: The poet voices the reader's question and answers it himself. Question: dropped the framing 'Forsitan et' and the governing verb 'quaeras' ('perhaps you also ask'), leaving the verbatim indirect interrogative 'scrobibus quae sint fastigia' normalized as a direct question (what depth the trenches should have). Answer: begins at the operative response 'ausim uel tenui uitem committere sulco' (shallow furrow suffices for the vine) and runs to the first full stop after 'tendit', covering the contrast that a tree by contrast is fixed deep. Stripped the inline verse number '290' that fell mid-passage. Stopped before line 293 ('ergo non hiemes illam...'), which digresses to the tree's endurance rather than answering the depth question.

question: Nam quis te, iuvenum confidentissime, nostras iussit adire domos? Quidve hinc petis?
answer: Deum praecepta secuti venimus hinc lapsis quaesitum oracula rebus.
derivation: Proteus, seized by Aristaeus, asks who sent him and what he seeks. Dropped the trailing speech tag 'inquit' (framing). In the reply, skipped the non-answering deflection 'Scis, Proteu, scis ipse; neque est te fallere quicquam sed tu desine velle.' (you already know, stop pretending) and took the operative answering sentence stating what he seeks; stops at the full stop ending the speech. Inline every-5-lines verse numbers (450) stripped; editorial quote marks normalized.

question: Cum sit perfectus Scripturarum Canon, sibique ad omnia satis superque sufficiat, quid opus est ut ei Ecclesiasticae intelligentiae jungatur auctoritas?
answer: Quia videlice Scripturam sacram pro ipsa sua altitudine non uno eodemque sensu universi accipiunt, sed ejusdem eloquia aliter atque aliter alius atque alius interpretatur; ut pene quot homines sunt, tot illinc sententiae erui posse videantur.
derivation: Question is the objection the author voices; dropped the framing tag 'Hic forsitan requirat aliquis:' that precedes it. Answer begins at 'Quia' and ends at the first full stop ('...erui posse videantur.'); the following 'Aliter namque illam Novatianus...' is illustrative elaboration, cut. 'videlice' kept verbatim as in source.

question: Quid igitur tunc faciet Christianus catholicus, si se aliqua Ecclesiae particula ab universalis fidei communione praeciderit?
answer: Quid utique nisi ut pestifero corruptoque membro sanitatem universi corporis anteponat?
derivation: Author poses the question and answers it himself with a 'quid utique nisi' reply that genuinely answers (he must prefer the health of the whole body). Both are contiguous and self-contained; nothing cut.

question: Quid si novella aliqua contagio non jam portiunculam tantum, sed totam pariter Ecclesiam commaculare conetur?
answer: Tunc item providebit ut antiquitati inhaereat, quae prorsum jam non potest ab ulla novitatis fraude seduci.
derivation: Conditional 'Quid si...?' question answered by the 'Tunc item providebit...' sentence that immediately opens line 30. Answer ends at the first full stop; the next sentence ('Quid si in ipsa vetustate...') begins the following pair, cut here.

question: Quid si in ipsa vetustate, duorum aut trium hominum, vel certe civitatis unius aut etiam provinciae alicujus error deprehendatur?
answer: Tunc omnino curabit ut paucorum temeritati vel inscitiae, si qua sunt, universaliter antiquitus universalis Ecclesiae decreta praeponat.
derivation: Conditional question directly answered by the following 'Tunc omnino curabit...' sentence. Stripped the scaffolding footnote marker '[5]' from within the answer ('universalis Ecclesiae [5] decreta' -> 'universalis Ecclesiae decreta'). Answer is a single full sentence; nothing further cut.

question: Quomodo in Trinitate alius atque alius, non aliud atque aliud?
answer: Quia scilicet alia et persona Patris, alia Filii, alia Spiritus sancti; sed tamen Patris et Filii et Spiritus sancti non alia et alia, sed una eademque natura.
derivation: Author's own self-posed 'Quomodo...?' question answered directly by the following 'Quia scilicet...' sentence (one full sentence, ending at the full stop). Self-contained; nothing cut.

question: Quomodo in Salvatore aliud atque aliud, non alius atque alius?
answer: Quia videlicet altera substantia divinitatis, altera humanitatis; sed tamen deitas et humanitas non alter et alter, sed unus idemque Christus, unus idemque filius Dei, et unius ejusdemque Christi et filii Dei una eademque persona; sicut in homine aliud caro, et aliud anima, sed unus idemque homo anima et caro.
derivation: Author's own self-posed 'Quomodo...?' question answered by the following 'Quia videlicet...' explanation, taken to its first full stop ('...anima et caro.'); the next sentence ('In Petro et Paulo...') is a further illustration, cut. Contiguous, no interior ellipsis.

question: Nullusne ergo in Ecclesia Christi profectus habebitur Religionis?
answer: Habeatur plane, et maximus.
derivation: Genuine interrogative (enclitic -ne) the author voices; dropped the framing 'Sed forsitan dicit aliquis:' that precedes it. Answer is the emphatic direct reply 'Habeatur plane, et maximus.'; the following 'Nam quis ille est tam invidus...' elaborates and is cut.

question: Quibusnam linguis potissimum danda sit opera?
answer: Eae autem duae sunt: graeca una, latina altera, utraque certa; sed graeca doctior; nunc latina communior.
derivation: The author poses the question via framing 'At heic quis vestrum roget:' which is dropped as asking-narration. The reply opens with a non-answering preamble (lines 46-47: 'Id vos docet ipsa corruptae naturae cognitio... Haec itaque vicia sunt emendanda linguarum eruditione, quae, quantum fieri possit, doctae sint, certae, communes...') that gives criteria but does not name which languages; so the answer's start is advanced to the operative naming sentence 'Eae autem duae sunt: graeca una, latina altera...' which directly answers 'which languages.' The answer ends at the first full stop (after 'communior'); what follows is 'His igitur a pueris incumbendum...', which turns to elaborating on how to study them.

question: Quid, quaeso, faceres, si tu esses?
answer: Ea perferrem, quae tu.
derivation: Direct-speech exchange. Dropped the narrative framing 'Nam cum quidam hostiam... causa exposita novissime conclusisset:' before the question and the speech tag 'ille respondit:' before the answer. The question is a genuine interrogative ('What, pray, would you do, if you were [him]?') and the answer ('I would endure those things which you [would]') directly answers it. Quoted both utterances verbatim and contiguous; no ellipsis.

question: Quid nunc faceret, si Domitiano supervixisset?
answer: Nobiscum cenaret.
derivation: Nerva asks Mauricus about Catullus the notorious informer (mentione Catulli facta, calumniatoris praecipui): 'What would he be doing now, had he survived Domitian?' Mauricus answers wittily that he would be dining with them. Dropped the framing 'dicente Nerva' before the question and 'inquit Mauricus' splitting the answer; normalized the answer's terminal punctuation. The question is a genuine verbatim interrogative and the answer directly responds to it.

question: Quomodo potest primus dici, post tantos, qui supra dicti sunt?
answer: Verum intelligemus primum pro principe, vel quia is ad perfectum illis temporibus circa peritiam medicae artis praecipuus fuisse traditur.
derivation: Authorial self-posed question about why Virgil writes 'primusque Machaon' after naming many others (Thessandrum, Sthenelum, Ulixem, etc.). Dropped the framing 'De quo quaeri potest:' (meta-narration of the asking) before the interrogative; capitalized 'Quomodo'. Answer is the author's own resolution beginning at 'Verum intelligemus' and running to the first full stop; the section then ends and 2,1 begins 'Sed ut ad propositum revertamur'.

question: Quem primum hasta, aut quem postremum bellica virgo demetis, aut quot humi candentia corpora linquis?
answer: Semianimes volvuntur equi niveique, nigrique, et peditum cunei, dilectaque pectora Marti aligera juvenes ineuntes bella sagitta.
derivation: The narrator apostrophizes the warrior-maiden (Amazon) with a genuine interrogative (quem... quem... quot...) at 370-371, ending at the question mark. He answers it himself, enumerating the slain she leaves on the ground, beginning at 372 'Semianimes volvuntur...'. The answer window ends at 374 'sagitta.', the last word before line 375 begins a new, separate rhetorical question ('Quis cladem fando illius...') which is the inexpressibility topos and is not answered. No scaffolding artifacts fall within the span.

question: O qui res hominumque deumque aeternis regis imperiis, et fulmine terres, quid meus Aeneas in te committere tantum, quid Troes potuere, quibus, tot funera passis, cunctus ob Italiam terrarum clauditur orbis? Certe hinc Romanos olim, volventibus annis, hinc fore ductores, revocato a sanguine Teucri, qui mare, qui terras omni dicione tenerent, pollicitus, quae te, genitor, sententia vertit? Hoc equidem occasum Troiae tristisque ruinas solabar, fatis contraria fata rependens; nunc eadem fortuna viros tot casibus actos insequitur. Quem das finem, rex magne, laborum? Antenor potuit, mediis elapsus Achivis, Illyricos penetrare sinus, atque intima tutus regna Liburnorum, et fontem superare Timavi, unde per ora novem vasto cum murmure montis it mare proruptum et pelago premit arva sonanti. Hic tamen ille urbem Patavi sedesque locavit Teucrorum, et genti nomen dedit, armaque fixit Troia; nunc placida compostus pace quiescit: nos, tua progenies, caeli quibus adnuis arcem, navibus (infandum!) amissis, unius ob iram prodimur atque Italis longe disiungimur oris. Hic pietatis honos? Sic nos in sceptra reponis?
answer: Parce metu, Cytherea: manent immota tuorum fata tibi; cernes urbem et promissa Lavini moenia, sublimemque feres ad sidera caeli magnanimum Aenean; neque me sententia vertit.
derivation: Whole-speech-as-question: Venus's entire address to Jupiter is one extended plea containing real interrogatives (quid meus Aeneas... potuere?; quae te... sententia vertit?; Quem das finem...?; Hic pietatis honos? Sic nos in sceptra reponis?). Dropped the framing 'adloquitur Venus:' before the speech; quoted from 'O qui res...' through '...in sceptra reponis?' contiguously, stripping the inline verse numbers 230/235/240/245/250 and normalizing the opening capital. Answer: dropped Jupiter's framing narration (Olli subridens... oscula libavit natae, dehinc talia fatur:) and began at the operative reassurance 'Parce metu, Cytherea'; ended at the first full stop after 'neque me sententia vertit.' (line 260), which directly answers Venus's 'quae te... sententia vertit?'. What follows the cut is Jupiter's digression 'Hic tibi (fabor enim...)... bellum ingens geret Italia...', a long prophecy that elaborates rather than answers, so it is excluded. Stripped inline numbers 255/260.

question: Quid uota furentem, quid delubra iuuant?
answer: Est mollis flamma medullas interea et tacitum uiuit sub pectore uulnus.
derivation: The poet asks what the prayers and shrines avail the raving Dido, then answers it himself: meanwhile the flame eats her soft marrow and the silent wound lives beneath her breast (i.e. they avail nothing). Question is the full interrogative at line 65-66. Answer ends at the first full stop (after uulnus); the preceding exclamation 'heu, uatum ignarae mentes!' (line 65) is framing/apostrophe and is dropped, and the following narration 'uritur infelix Dido...' begins a new sentence and is excluded. Stripped inline verse number 65 and the dangling 70/75 markers.

question: Dissimulare etiam sperasti, perfide, tantum posse nefas tacitusque mea decedere terra? nec te noster amor nec te data dextera quondam nec moritura tenet crudeli funere Dido? quin etiam hiberno moliri sidere classem et mediis properas Aquilonibus ire per altum, crudelis? quid, si non arua aliena domosque ignotas peteres, et Troia antiqua maneret, Troia per undosum peteretur classibus aequor? mene fugis? per ego has lacrimas dextramque tuam te (quando aliud mihi iam miserae nihil ipsa reliqui), per conubia nostra, per inceptos hymenaeos, si bene quid de te merui, fuit aut tibi quicquam dulce meum, miserere domus labentis et istam, oro, si quis adhuc precibus locus, exue mentem. te propter Libycae gentes Nomadumque tyranni odere, infensi Tyrii; te propter eundem exstinctus pudor et, qua sola sidera adibam, fama prior. cui me moribundam deseris hospes (hoc solum nomen quoniam de coniuge restat)? quid moror? an mea Pygmalion dum moenia frater destruat aut captam ducat Gaetulus Iarbas? saltem si qua mihi de te suscepta fuisset ante fugam suboles, si quis mihi paruulus aula luderet Aeneas, qui te tamen ore referret, non equidem omnino capta ac deserta uiderer.
answer: Sed nunc Italiam magnam Gryneus Apollo, Italiam Lyciae iussere capessere sortes; hic amor, haec patria est.
derivation: Dido's whole utterance (305-330) is quoted verbatim and contiguous as the question; it is one extended accusation/plea with genuine interrogatives (mene fugis?, nec te... tenet... Dido?). The framing 'tandem his Aenean compellat uocibus ultro' (304) is dropped as narration. Aeneas's reply (333-361) opens with a non-answering preamble: 'ego te... numquam, regina, negabo promeritam... neque ego hanc abscondere furto speraui... nec coniugis umquam praetendi taedas... me si fata meis paterentur... colerem, Priami tecta alta manerent...' (333-344) acknowledges her merits and a counterfactual but does not answer why he leaves. Answer-start advanced to 'sed nunc Italiam magnam...' (345), the operative answering sentence stating his fated reason for departure; cut at the full stop after 'hic amor, haec patria est.' (347), where he turns to the further rhetorical 'si te Karthaginis arces... inuidia est?' digression. The speech-tag 'tandem pauca refert' and the bracketed line 261 verse number scaffolding are excluded; no editorial angle brackets occur in the quoted spans.

question: Cognoscis illum, qui percussus est ab angelo et vulneratus ad mortem?
answer: Domine, nescio, nec locum cognosco.
derivation: In the dream-vision the angel directly asks Charles whether he recognizes the man (the Dauphin) struck down for the sin of luxuria, and Charles answers directly. Stripped the framing speech tags 'Tunc tenens nos per capillos angelus dixit:' before the question and 'Tunc diximus:' before the answer. The question is self-contained ('illum, qui percussus est ab angelo et vulneratus ad mortem' supplies its own referent). Answer ends at the full stop; what follows ('Dixit: Scire debes...') is the angel's next, separate explanatory speech, not part of the reply.

question: Intellexistis hec omnia?
answer: Eciam.
derivation: Within the Gospel exposition the author quotes Christ's question and the disciples' reply; the text itself flags it: 'Interrogatoria sunt hec verba.' Stripped the speech tag 'Dicunt ei:' between question and answer. The answer 'Eciam' is the disciples' whole direct reply; what follows ('Unde cum dominus proposuisset...') is the author's commentary, not part of the utterance.

question: Quid ita sol quinto a se signo potius quam secundo aut tertio, quae sunt propiora, facit in his fervoribus retentiones?
answer: Eius radii in mundo uti trigoni paribus lateribus formae liniationibus extenduntur. Id autem nec plus nec minus est ad quintum ab eo signo.
derivation: Authorial-rhetorical Q&A. Stripped the framing 'Fortasse desiderabitur,' (= 'perhaps it will be asked', narration of the question, analogous to 'fortasse requiris') and normalized the first word's capitalization ('quid' -> 'Quid') and terminal punctuation to '?'. For the answer, skipped the non-answering preamble 'Ergo, quemadmodum id fieri videatur, exponam.' (a mere announcement that he will explain) and started at the operative answering sentences explaining why the retention is at the fifth sign: the sun's rays extend in the form of an equilateral triangle, which falls exactly at the fifth sign. Stopped before 'Igitur si radii per omnem mundum fusi...', which elaborates a counterfactual rather than continuing the direct answer.

locus: Iacobus de Voragine, De Sancto Andrea Apostolo (resurrection of the young man at Nicaea)
question: Quid dabis mihi, si suscitavero filium tuum?
answer: Nil carius ego possidebam, ipsum ergo tibi dabo.
derivation: Andreas asks the father a genuine interrogative; the father answers directly. Dropped the speech tags 'Dixitque patri:' before and 'Cui ille:' before the answer. Normalized terminal punctuation (added '?'; the source lacks a closing quote/question mark after 'filium tuum').

locus: Iacobus de Voragine, De Sancto Andrea Apostolo (Episcopus atque Diabolus, first riddle)
question: Quod est maius mirabile, quod Deus umquam in parva re fecerit?
answer: Diversitas et excellentia facierum.
derivation: The woman (devil) proposes the riddle; the peregrinus (Andreas) answers. Question: dropped the asking-frame 'Interrogetur,' before 'quod est maius mirabile'; normalized capitalization and terminal '?'. Answer: kept only the first answering sentence to the first full stop; cut at the colon, omitting the following elaboration 'Inter tot enim homines... Deus collocavit.' Dropped the answer's speech tag 'Interrogatus de hoc peregrinus per nuntium dixit:'.

locus: Iacobus de Voragine, De Sancto Andrea Apostolo (Episcopus atque Diabolus, second riddle)
question: Ubi terra sit altior omni coelo?
answer: In coelo empyreo, ubi residet corpus Christi.
derivation: Question: dropped the asking-frame 'Proponatur sibi secunda quaestio gravior, in qua melius possumus sapientiam eius experiri: Quaeratur ab eo,' before 'ubi terra sit altior omni coelo'; normalized capitalization and terminal '?'. Answer: kept the first answering sentence to the first full stop; cut before the explanatory elaboration 'Corpus enim Christi... terra altior coelo manet.' Dropped the speech tag 'Percunctatus de hoc peregrinus respondit:'.

locus: Iacobus de Voragine, De Sancto Andrea Apostolo (Episcopus atque Diabolus, third riddle)
question: Quanti spatii sit a terra usque in coelum?
answer: Vade ad eum, qui te misit ad me et de hoc diligenter percunctare.
derivation: Question: dropped the asking-frame 'Fiet ei tertia quaestio gravissima... Quaeratur ab eo,' before 'quanti spatii sit a terra usque in coelum'; normalized capitalization and terminal '?'. Answer: kept the operative deflecting answer (the riddle's point, that the devil himself measured the distance when he fell) to the first full stop; cut before 'Ipse enim melius me hoc novit... in similitudinem mulieris.' Dropped the speech tag 'Requisitus de hoc peregrinus nuntio dixit:'.

locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Antonio
question: Ubi eras, bone Iesu? Ubi eras? Quare non a principio fuisti hic, ut me adiuvares et vulnera mea sanares?
answer: Antoni, hic eram, sed exspectabam videre certamen tuum.
derivation: Antony asks the just-arrived Christ where he was; the Lord answers directly. Dropped framing 'Ibique Christum adesse intellegens ait' before and 'Cui Dominus:' before the reply. Answer window ends at the first full stop ('certamen tuum:'), cutting the colon-joined elaboration that follows ('Nunc autem, quia viriliter dimicasti, in toto orbe te faciam nominare'). Normalized exclamation marks to question marks.

locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Antonio
question: O quis istos evadet?
answer: Humilitas.
derivation: While rapt in spirit Antony sees the world full of snares and cries out a question; a voice answers one word. Dropped framing 'Qui exclamans ait:' and 'Et audivit:'. Normalized terminal '!' to '?'.

locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Antonio
question: Cur me sic impugnant monachi et maledicunt Christiani?
answer: Iuste hoc faciunt, quia tuis saepe insidiis molestantur.
derivation: Satan asks Antony why monks attack and Christians curse him; Antony answers directly. Dropped framing 'addidit satanas:' before and 'Cui Antonius:' before the reply. Answer ends at the first full stop, before the next speaker turn ('Et ille:'). Normalized terminal '!' to '?'.

Corpus enim meum penitus tibi trado.' elaborates the defiance rather than answering, so the window stops at the first full stop.
